## Process: SR from another nucleus; field drift correction after Najbauer & Andreas (2026-10-01)

- **Asked**: (1) in Process ▸ Reference, a calculator giving the SR of one nucleus from the SR calibrated on another, `SR_new = (SR_cal / SFO1_cal) × SFO1_new`, copyable, with a warning that it holds only on the same magnet at a similar time; (2) field drift correction in Process, translating the two TopSpin AU programs of E. E. Najbauer & L. B. Andreas, *J. Magn. Reson.* 305 (2019) 1–4, doi:10.1016/j.jmr.2019.05.005 (`lindriftcomp`, `concatenate_ser_nuslist`), with the citation.
- **Built -- SR transfer**: `notebook/referencing.py` (`transfer_sr`, `transfer_sr_between`, `spectrum_sr_hz`, `VALIDITY_WARNING`). With no SFO1_new it estimates one from the γ ratio (flagged: bare γ ≠ IUPAC Ξ, ~1e-4 for 13C/1H, up to ~1 % for heavy nuclei -- of the SR, so sub-Hz). Warns when SFO1_new/SFO1_cal disagrees with the two nuclei's γ ratio by > 2 % (a number from the wrong experiment) and on |correction| > 5 ppm. GUI: Reference ▸ "SR from Another Nucleus" (collapsible): fill SR_cal/SFO1_cal from an open experiment (its SR *in effect*, same rule as the SR box) or by hand; SFO1_new from the selected spectrum, direct or indirect; Copy SR_new; Apply to This Spectrum (logged with the numbers). Note: SR/SFO1 vs SR/BF1 differ by O1/BF1 (~1e-4 of SR, mHz) -- the user's formula is kept.
- **Built -- drift correction**: `notebook/drift_correction.py`. One code path for planes / points / NUS and QF / States / States-TPPI / Echo-Antiecho: `acquisition_layout` works out which FIDs make up each hypercomplex point in acquisition order (read off the AU's own index arithmetic -- planes `[k_out][b_out][k_in][b_in]`, points/NUS `[k...][b_out][b_in]`, AQSEQ 321/312, 4D 4321; F1 = the highest-numbered `acquNs`), then `apply_drift_correction` applies `exp(i2πΔt2)` (t2 from the end of the group delay) and, per indirect dimension, θ = 2πΔ(BF_d/BF_dir)t_d as a cos/sin rotation (States), `exp(∓iθ)` on echo/antiecho (EA), or `exp(−iθ)` (QF). `correct_bruker_dataset` writes a new EXPNO (int32 or float64, byte order kept, audit file `opennmr_drift_correction.txt`); `concatenate_nus_datasets` joins blocks into a new EXPNO and updates NusPOINTS; `measure_drift_hz` gives reference − observed from 1D spectra, compared by frequency (δ·SF + SR), so different SRs do not read as drift; sub-point via a parabola. `io.bruker.read_2d(drift_correction={...})` corrects a 2D/pseudo-2D on load: `fid_raw` is then the *corrected* FIDs (every in-memory reprocess starts from it) and `fid_raw_uncorrected` the file's, which `Session._load_with` now hands back as `_raw_fid_cache` -- otherwise a reprocess would correct twice (tested). Saved with the processing state; `_saved_processing_read_kwargs` reads it back as a reader kwarg; history labels it.
- **GUI**: Process ▸ Field Drift Correction (`gui/drift_panel.py`): 1. measure (reference / before / after 1D, ppm region); 2. start/end shifts; 3. Apply to Selected Spectrum (a reload with `drift_correction`, carrying over SR, baseline, F1 phase etc. and re-applying them via `_apply_loaded_processing_sidecar`), Remove Correction, Write Corrected Bruker Dataset… (3D/4D/NUS too), Concatenate NUS Blocks…; citation with DOI link.
- **Verified**: the port against the AU's own loops written out in the tests (3D planes 321, 3D NUS, 2D EA via the AU's EA→States mapping), `endpoint=False`; end-to-end through `read_2d` for QF/States/States-TPPI/EA and pseudo-2D -- a drifting synthetic peak restored to correlation > 0.999 with the undrifted one, the wrong sign makes it worse, F2-only correction leaves an F1 smear. The signs were *measured* through openNMR's reader (Bruker raw `e^{+i2πft2}` reads at +f; QF F1 `e^{+i2πft1}` reads at −f; the AU's EA mapping decodes to the same F1 as States). **Not verified on real drifting data** -- none was available; do that before relying on 3D/4D or EA 3D/4D (EA beyond 2D is not in the AU program).
- **Deliberate differences from the AU programs** (in the module docstring): last FID gets the end shift exactly (`endpoint=False` reproduces the AU's `p/P`); points mode uses the full elapsed index for the direct dimension too (the AU uses only the slow loop counter there); the AU's 2D QF branch has `arg2 == 0` (a comparison, so unless IN_F is 0, QF row pairs are rotated into each other -- on a pseudo-2D, neighbouring slices mixed); EA is phased in place rather than converted to States + FnMODE rewritten; genuine QF 2D gets its F1 correction; nothing is overwritten (the concatenation AU appends onto the first dataset). F1 dwell is 1/SW_h of that dimension (= IN_F for QF/States/EA). Not handled: TPPI/QSEQ (FnMODE 2/3; refused with the reason), a non-zero initial t1 (d0; as the AU), drift within a 1D's accumulation (impossible; refused).
- **Open**: a time-based ramp (from the 1D spectra's own acquisition times rather than FID index) for when the before/after 1Ds are not right next to the nD; a non-linear (measured per block) drift from several interleaved 1Ds -- `shifts_hz` already accepts it, the GUI does not.

## DNP rebuilt as a step-by-step workflow in Apply ▸ DNP; multi-select Remove; plot style follows the plot kind (2026-09-30, round 2)

- **Asked**: (1) Remove removes every selected spectrum in Open experiments; (2) DNP Enhancement and Field Sweep Profile move to Apply ▸ DNP, two sub-sections; (3) plot style adapts to the plot: 1D spectra (fits, simulations) always "1-d", 2D "2-d", profiles/curves "Curve or Profile"; (4) the field sweep was unclear -- rebuild it as: B0 per spectrum from nucleus + SFO1; pick a reference and a line, align every spectrum to it (receiver offset may change, so position is not to be trusted; match shape/width/normalised points); inspect, drag to correct in a Compare-like stacked/superimposed view, confirm (each spectrum its own SR); integrate a region and/or pick a shift on the reference; plot vs B0 as absolute (per scan) or enhancement (ON/OFF, or 1 − ON/OFF). Enhancement calculator: the same steps, then the enhancement, height and integral both encouraged.
- **What was wrong**: Remove took only `currentRow()`. Several views never announced a plot kind (`show_slice_fit` -- every spectral/CSA/quad fit --, 2D overlay/panels, heatmap, DOSY, the Czjzek map, kept-fit comparisons), so the canvas kept whatever kind it last showed (often "curve") and the saved default for the right kind was never applied; Plot Style's Per-type combo never followed the plot at all.
- **Built**:
  - `_on_remove_clicked` removes every selected row (last first, `_after_session_row_removed` each); the context menu offers "Remove N Selected" when the clicked row is part of a selection.
  - Canvas views announce `1d`/`2d`/`pseudo2d`; kept-fit comparisons of spectra `1d`, Czjzek map `2d`, DNP single spectrum `1d`, aligned set `compare`, profile `curve`. `_follow_plot_kind` sets Plot Style ▸ Per-type defaults to the kind on show (and the scope label names it). Multi-spectrum Compare views stay "Compare" (a type of its own).
  - `notebook/dnp_workflow.py` (the maths; `dnp.py` kept for existing notebooks): `spectrum_fields` (B0 = SFO1/γ), `align_spectra`, `set_manual_shift`, `shift_for_display_ppm`, `aligned_spectrum(s)` (ppm with its own reference ν0_i = ν_line,i/(1+δ_ref); Hz axis kept, so integrals are untouched), `alignment_fields` (B0 at the line, or from SFO1, with their difference), `measure` (height and/or integral via `dnp.peak_height`/`region_integral`; noise errors, systematic from baseline window ±1 FWHM / region ±20%, RG scaled to the reference, per scan), `field_profile` (absolute / ratio / one_minus vs an OFF spectrum, sorted by field, OFF optionally excluded), `enhancement_table` (ON/OFF and 1 − ON/OFF by height and integral, agreement within 2σ), reports, CSV, `plot_aligned_spectra`, `plot_field_profile`.
  - **Alignment algorithm** (the user was unsure how): on the carrier-offset axis (Hz), the reference line ±3 FWHM is the template; each spectrum is searched ±20 kHz with a sliding correlation in which *each window is detrended by its own straight line* (so a line on a broad feature's flank or a rolled baseline still matches); |r| is used, so inverted lines are found (sign reported). Among matches within 0.15 of the best |r|, the one whose FWHM is closest to the reference's wins -- a taller broad hump 7 kHz away was matched before these two changes (tested). Accepted at |r| ≥ 0.6 and S/N ≥ 5; otherwise left at the reference's carrier offset and flagged (a zero-crossing of the profile has nothing to find). The reference line's centre is a least-squares parabola over its top ±FWHM/3 (a three-point vertex wandered half a point = ~0.5 µT for 23Na). Widths are measured above a line through ±2.5 FWHM. Tested to ≤ 3 Hz with carriers moved by up to 12 kHz and different SW/sizes.
  - **Fields**: both SFO1 (asked for) and at-the-line are computed; the GUI defaults to the line and reports how far apart they are (up to 2.6 mT in a test sweep). The absolute field depends on the reference line's ppm (δ_ref); field differences do not.
  - `gui/dnp_panel.py` now holds `DnpWorkflowPanel(mode="sweep"|"enhancement")` (numbered steps 1–5, later steps reset when an earlier one changes, measuring locked until the alignment is confirmed) and `DnpAlignDialog` (matplotlib window: press on a trace, drag, release = hand shift; stacked/superimposed; reset; confirm). The old `DnpPanel` is gone (the Compare tile has only Arithmetic now). Results kept in `metadata.raw["fits"]["dnp_sweep"/"dnp_enhancement"]` as before. Stacked rows are spaced by each trace's span, so inverted lines do not run into the row below.
- **Tests**: `test_dnp_workflow.py` (15), `test_gui_dnp.py` (rewritten, 9), `test_gui_remove_and_plot_kinds.py` (5); updated for the move/new behaviour: `test_gui_compare_tools.py`, `test_gui_export_scroll.py`, `test_gui_legend_style.py` and `test_gui_usability.py` (the DNP 1D-style, curve-style, palette, Home and crosshair contracts, now through the new workflow), `test_gui.py` (Remove removes every selected row -- `_remove_rows` is the single-row path now; Apply's sections include DNP). Also updated to the 2026-09-30 re-wording commits, which had broken them on `main`: `test_cpmg.py` (VOCS section title) and two `test_gui.py` fit-report CSV headers.
- **Bug caught by the ported tests**: the profile read the plot style *before* the Fit view switched to the "curve" default, so its first draw used the previous plot's colours; styles are now read inside the draw.
- **Not done / next**: keyboard nudging in the drag window; a sweep with several lines (one line is tracked); the SimulationCanvas (Bloch, diffusion, tensor pictures) is plain matplotlib and outside Plot Style.

## Herzfeld-Berger skew = 3(δ22 − δiso)/Ω; manual baselines (quartic / sine) in notebook and GUI (2026-09-29, round 4)

- **Asked**: (1) make the Herzfeld-Berger skew the standard definition, κ = 3(δ22 − δiso)/Ω; (2) "make a baseline manually" by fitting A x⁴ + B x³ + C x² + D x + E or A sin(B x + C) + D, correctable in the GUI.
- **What was wrong**: `herzfeld_berger_csa_tensor` and `convert_csa_parameters` used κ = 3(δiso − δ22)/Ω -- the *opposite* sign to Herzfeld-Berger/Mason. The old changelog item 3 in `notebook/simulations.py` called that sign a "fix"; it was the bug. Every HB skew entered, fitted or converted had its sign flipped (κ = +1 gave δ22 = δ33 instead of δ22 = δ11). Now δ22 = δiso + Ωκ/3. **Saved states, sidecars and notebooks holding HB skew values from before this change describe the mirror-image tensor: negate κ to keep the old tensor.** Haeberlen was unaffected. `tests/test_gui_round4_transfers.py` pinned the old sign (−0.529412) and now uses +0.529412 (worked by hand: principal 66, 34, −70 ppm).
- **Built**:
  - `notebook/manual_baseline.py` (exported from `opennmr.notebook`): `fit_manual_baseline(x, y, model, regions, fixed, initial)` (polynomial: exact column-scaled linear least squares; sine: FFT/trial-frequency linear solve for the start, then `curve_fit`, reported with A, B ≥ 0, C in (−π, π]); 1σ errors; `evaluate_manual_baseline`, `manual_baseline_correct` (on notebook result dicts), `plot_manual_baseline`, `describe_manual_baseline`. x is ppm; no sigma-clipping (the regions are the user's statement of where the baseline is); with no regions, the first/last 5 %.
  - `processing.ft.compute_baseline`/`baseline_correct` methods `"manual_polynomial"`/`"manual_sine"` with `manual_params` (evaluated as given), `manual_refit` (fit to `baseline_regions` on every trace), `manual_fixed`.
  - GUI: two entries in Process ▸ Baseline ▸ method; `gui/manual_baseline_box.py` (`ManualBaselineBox`, `parse_regions`) under it: regions line + "Pick on plot" (drag on the Processing preview; uses the canvas's existing region-select mode, released like any other mode), coefficient boxes with ± and Fix, "Fit to regions" (fits the trace *before* correction -- the pipeline's stash, else the spectrum/selected slice), "Refit on every trace". Hand edits switch Refit off (a plain focus change does not). State in `metadata.raw`: `baseline_manual_regions`, `baseline_manual_{polynomial,sine}_{params,fixed}` (per model, so switching keeps both), `baseline_manual_refit` -- so the toggle, overlay, every-slice path, sidecar and restore-on-reselect all work as for the automatic methods. Regions shaded green on the preview (`MplCanvas.set_baseline_regions`). Warnings: no regions, a region with signal, a region with no points, too few points. Methods report (`processing/report.py`) and history log state the equation, coefficients and regions.
  - CSA tooltips (`CSA_ANISOTROPY_TIP`, `CSA_ASYMMETRY_TIP` in `notebook/simulations.py`) state both conventions' definitions on the Simulate/Fit CSA and Combined panels.
- **Not done**: a manual baseline is not offered for the F1 dimension of a genuine 2D, beyond what the existing baseline targeting already does; no drag-to-edit of the curve itself (coefficients are typed).
- Tests: `tests/test_manual_baseline.py` (26, incl. HB skew), `tests/test_gui_manual_baseline.py` (22). Full suite: 3144 passed, 164 skipped, 1 pre-existing Czjzek failure (see top).

- **(3) Built**: `notebook/czjzek.py`. P(C_Q, η_Q) of the Gaussian isotropic model, normalised exactly for any d (`N = Γ(d/2)/2 (2σ²)^(d/2) J(d)`), = the published d = 5 form (d'Espinose de Lacaillerie et al., JMR 2008). Spectrum = Σ cell-integrated P × lineshape, then δiso-spread broadening and shift. Lineshapes via `CzjzekLibrary`: **scaling** -- CT at second order scales exactly as C_Q², so one powder set per η_Q serves every C_Q (static exact; under MAS the rotor-averaged centreband, used only when a full simulation at the 99th-percentile C_Q puts < 2 % of the CT in sidebands) -- else **simulated** per grid point with `quadrupolar_spectrum` (seconds static, minutes MAS; the GUI asks first). `fit_czjzek_spectrum` (sites δiso, σ, d [held at 5 unless freed], FWHM, amplitude, L fraction; bounds/fixed as the quad fit; fits once on a grid sized to the bounds, then again on a grid sized to the fitted σ), `czjzek_fit_report` (⟨C_Q⟩, C_Q mode, ⟨η_Q⟩, ⟨P_Q⟩, CT centre of gravity; errors propagate exactly since averages scale with σ), warnings for a tail off the axis / bounds / too few cells. `plot_czjzek_distribution` / `plot_czjzek_fit`: heat map + colour bar (own grid slot, so tight_layout and the GUI label pass work) + spectrum to the right or above; ⟨C_Q⟩,⟨η_Q⟩ marked; each site outlined at half maximum in its component's colour. GUI (`gui/czjzek_panels.py`): Fit ▸ "Quadrupolar (Czjzek distribution)" (`CzjzekFitPanel` subclasses `QuadrupolarFitPanel`, whose table constants became class attributes), results table, Show Fit / Show Distribution Map (layout, all sites by area or one), saved/logged as fit "czjzek", Send to Simulate; Simulate ▸ "Czjzek distribution" (`CzjzekSimPanel`: draws the map + spectrum on the Simulation plot, journalled, Add to Open Experiments).
- **Checked against independent results**: normalisation (d = 3, 5, 7.5) by 2-D quadrature; ⟨C_Q²(1+η²/3)⟩ = dσ² and ⟨η_Q⟩ = 0.61; scaling library = full static simulator to 1e-13, = MAS centreband to 2e-3; simulated spectra's CT centre of gravity = δiso + ⟨second-order shift⟩ (static and MAS, 0.02 ppm); a two-site fit recovers σ to 0.5 %, δiso to 0.05 ppm.
- **Found on the way**: `show_slice_fit` callers sometimes pass more labels than components; the canvas now trims/pads (the notebook function stays strict).
- **Not done**: the extended Czjzek model (a mean EFG tensor plus a Czjzek part) and mixing Czjzek with discrete sites in one fit; component styles are not saved with the plot-style defaults.

## T1/T2 with CSA, quadrupolar and Combined-Hamiltonian lineshapes: fit every slice (2026-09-28)

- **Asked**: fitting a slice of a pseudo-2D T1/T2 series with a CSA/quad (or mixed) model left "Export to pseudo-2D" greyed out, so T1/T2 could not be fitted with those models.
- **What was wrong**: nothing was broken -- the feature did not exist. Those three fits only ever covered one slice; the CSA export button was deliberately disabled for good ("until CSA fitting gains its own multi-slice workflow"), and quadrupolar/combined had none. Fit Curve only reads `slice_fit_results`, which only Fit Spectrum/Integrate Regions wrote.
- **Built**:
  - `notebook/series_fitting.py` (exported from `opennmr.notebook`): `model_components(kind, fit)` -- per-site fitted curves from a CSA/quadrupolar/combined fit; `fit_series_with_lineshapes(pseudo2d, x, components, labels, rows, fit_regions, baseline)` -- each slice fitted as a *linear* combination of those fixed site shapes + a linear baseline (lstsq; errors from s^2 (A^T A)^-1; amplitudes signed, so inversion recovery works); `series_fit_report`. Results use the `slice_fit_results` shape (`index`, `slice`, `x`, `y`, `y_fit`) plus `integrals` (signed site areas) / `amplitudes` (relative to the reference slice) with errors, `site_labels`, `model`, `model_fit=True`.
  - `processing.relaxation.NMR2D_fit_relaxation` reads model series: `value_source="area"` -> `integrals`, `"amplitude"` -> `amplitudes`; curves labelled by site.
  - GUI: a "Pseudo-2D series (T1, T2, …)" box under Fit ▸ CSA/Dipolar, Quadrupolar and Combined Hamiltonian -- "Fit Every Slice with this … Model" (live once that section has fitted a slice of the selected pseudo-2D; each fit now records its `row`, and combined its `fit_regions`), and "Export … Fit to Pseudo-2D…" (live once the staged series is that model's). Stages for Dynamics ▸ Fit Curve (Value source steered off "region"), records `fits["series_<kind>"]` with the report (logged, saved), flags R² < 0.9 slices. `export_csa_pseudo2d_button` is kept as the CSA box's export button. The fit-report CSV lists model series per slice per site (and no longer assumes every staged result has `popt` -- an integration series would have raised there).
- **Checked**: two CSA sites, inversion recovery, T1 0.15/0.9 s on a sloping baseline with noise -> both T1s within 3% through the real CSA fit and the real Fit Curve button; quadrupolar CT T2 within 3%; Monte Carlo (300 realisations) -- reported amplitude errors match the scatter within 15%.
- **Existing work reused / not**: `notebook/csa_relaxation.NMR2D_fit_csa_slices` already had the same frozen-shape linear method, CSA only, from notebook dicts, fitting its own reference slice, and amplitudes >= 0 by default (wrong for inversion recovery unless `allow_negative_intensity=True`). Left as is; `series_fitting` generalises the method to all three models from a fit already made, and says so.

## Adiabatic pulses in the Bloch simulator; 3D tensor pictures (2026-09-27)

User: add adiabatic shapes (tanh/tan, WURST, hyperbolic secant) to the Bloch simulator; visualise the simulated tensors (CSA, quadrupolar, both) "as ellipsoids? ... an isotropic shift would be a sphere of radius delta_iso. J would modify the isotropic sphere... not certain".

- **Adiabatic shapes** (`simulate/bloch.py`): `adiabatic_shape` (HSn, WURST-n, tanh/tan; amplitude + frequency sweep -SW/2..+SW/2, phase = running integral), routed by `simulate_pulse(..., sweep_width_hz, adiabatic_params)`. `generate_shape` untouched (exact copy of the pulse-programme function). Sweep limited to +/-500 kHz (1 point/us). Sign convention and time-step convergence tested.
- **Power by adiabaticity Q0** (`peak_b1_for_adiabaticity`): Q at the centre crossing, the literature parameter; `adiabaticity()` also reports the worst crossing-Q over 80% of the sweep; the GUI reports the simulated inverted band at each power scale -- the arbiter. Rejected: power from the worst crossing-Q (538 kHz of B1 for tanh/tan) and the global min |omega_eff|/|dtheta/dt| (falls as B1 rises, too pessimistic).

Glyphs: CSA ellipsoid |delta_ii| (flagged when signs are mixed), EFG principal axes (traceless: never an ellipsoid), in one frame.
- **J**: isotropic J changes no shape -- it copies the whole surface at each multiplet offset; drawn as wireframes when visible, otherwise explained in the notes. Anisotropic J has the dipolar form, not in the simulator.

## DNP: enhancement factors and field-sweep profiles (2026-09-27)

User: a "DNP" collapsible box in Compare (and notebook functions): (1) the enhancement factor as the ratio of two picked peak intensities *and* of two integrated regions -- encourage both, force neither; (2) for a DNP field sweep, the field of each experiment from SFO1 and the nucleus's gyromagnetic ratio, and a picked peak's intensity or a dragged region's area tracked against field. Example: `400_MHz_Lyon/20260511_Na2CdMnFeCN6_171025A_DR_3p2mm/100236-100305` (23Na).

- **SFO1 does not follow the line exactly.** It is set by hand: the line sat -7.6 to +13.8 kHz off its carrier (up to 1.26 mT for 23Na) against ~0.4 mT BSMS steps and a ~1.1 kHz line; SFO1 alone put 100288 below 100287. So the line is **found in every spectrum** (largest signal within ±window of the pick, on each spectrum's carrier-offset axis) and **B0 comes from the line's absolute frequency**; the SFO1 field is always reported alongside with the difference, and used only (flagged) where no line is found (S/N < 5 or maximum outside the window -- a noise maximum is never reported as a peak). Real-data checks: repeats agree to 7 uT (100267-69) and 26 uT (100300/04/05); 100287 < 100288 < 100289.
- Absolute field needs the line's shift (nu = gamma B0 (1 + delta)): default read off the reference spectrum's ppm axis at the line; overridable. Moves the whole profile by 1e-6 per ppm, never its shape.
- `metadata.sfo1` is SF (the ppm reference), **not** the carrier: DNP reads acqus SFO1 (fallback BF1 + O1). Data are per scan (readers divide by NS); RG is not normalised by the readers, so DNP corrects it (default on). TopSpin 1r files are not comparable across expnos (NC_proc -9..-13) and are not used.
- **Baseline: local quadratic by default.** 100268/100269 (uw on/off) has a rolling baseline; global (Quantify's edge line) gave eps = 1.13 height / 1.18 area, none 1.24 / 1.52, local 1.10 / 1.07. Rejected: a *straight* local line (cut an area by a third under a curved baseline in testing), and ±3 FWHM for a peak's baseline window (Lorentzian tail 2.7% -> heights 2% low; now ±5 FWHM).
- **Noise**: MAD of the residual about a 101-point quadratic Savitzky-Golay smooth. Rejected: edge SD (inflated ~20x by the roll) and point-to-point differences (~18% low: zero-filling correlates neighbours, lag-1 rho 0.4-0.6).
- **Enhancement uncertainty has a systematic term** (ratio change with the peak's baseline window ±4/±6 FWHM and the region 20% narrower/wider): changing the region moved the area ratio ~10x its noise error. The height-vs-area agreement check uses noise + systematic.
- Warns when a sweep mixes pulse programmes (this one: hahnecho4.enb and presat_zg).

## CI failure: label-shrink test broke on matplotlib 3.11 (2026-09-27)

User: GitHub Actions `Tests` run showed one `F` at ~55% and stopped at 72% with no summary.

- The `F` was `tests/test_gui_canvas.py::test_canvas_shrinks_labels_rather_than_clipping_them` (found by lining up CI's pass/skip pattern against a local run). CI does a fresh `pip install`, so it got **matplotlib 3.11.2**; local environments were on 3.10.x.
- The code was fine. The test assumed a 1.4 x 0.9 in canvas can't hold the 16 pt x label, so `fit_labels_within_figure` would have to shrink it. On 3.10 `tight_layout` gives up at that size, but on 3.11 it fits the label (123 px wide in a 140 px figure), so nothing shrank and `assert 16.0 < 16` failed.
- Fix: the test now uses 1.1 x 0.9 in, where the full-size label is **wider than the figure**, so geometry forces the shrink whatever the layout engine does. The test checks that premise itself and fails with a clear message if a future change breaks it. Settles at 13.6 pt on both versions.
- CI stopping at 72% with no summary means the job was **cancelled**, either by `timeout-minutes: 30` or by `cancel-in-progress` when a newer push arrived. Check the run's annotation. If it was the timeout, the suite has outgrown 30 min on the runner; options are a higher timeout or `pytest-xdist` (`-n auto`), which would need checking against the Qt/offscreen fixtures.

## Multi-spectrum fitting: series, isotopes, fields (2026-09-26, fourth round)

User: *"three main cases: 1. sequential data (variable-temperature or variable-time) ... the best fit values from the first spectrum should feed into the second ... 2. different isotopes of the same material, e.g. 1H and 2H ... 3. the same isotope at different fields. For 2 and 3 there may be differences in MAS frequency and field. Fit, consistently, the same set of peaks across the datasets ... any number of experiments with any numbers in any order (e.g. 5, 302, 12, 2, 49)."*

Design (not yet reviewed by the user -- check against real data): one engine on the Combined-Hamiltonian model (an isotropic line is a site with no interactions); **scopes** per parameter (per experiment / per nucleus / global); series = sequential seeding **plus** optional global parameters refined jointly; isotopes share δiso with an optional fitted **per-isotope δ offset**; across fields the linewidth is **split into Hz + ppm**; a new Fit section.

### Built
- **`notebook/multi_fitting.py`** (exported from `opennmr.notebook`): `make_experiment` (per-spectrum nucleus, ν0, MAS, order, transitions, orientations, window, baseline, x value), `fit_multi(experiments, sites_by_nucleus, scopes=, amounts=, vary=, fixed=, bounds=, seed=, joint=, preset=, progress=)`, `default_scopes(preset)` (series / isotopes / fields), `multi_fit_table`, `parameter_trend`, `multi_fit_to_csv`, `print_multi_fit_report`, `plot_multi_fit`, `plot_parameter_trend`, `MultiFitCancelled`.
  - **Links** (`_Map`): a shared parameter is one key; each experiment's value comes through a link: identity; **C_Q scaled by |Q| ratio** (the EFG is shared; η_Q identical); **J scaled by γ_A·γ_X** (reduced coupling isotope-independent; J groups matched by index); δiso + per-nucleus **offset** (held at 0 unless varied); **width** = width_Hz/ν0(MHz) ⊕ width_ppm (quadrature for Gaussian, linear otherwise); **amount** = shared site amount × per-experiment scale (the first experiment's scale in each group held at 1 -- otherwise degenerate).
  - **Sequential pass first, always**: `fit_combined` per experiment in the given order, seeded from the last fit of the same site (same nucleus; else the chemical parameters of another nucleus's last fit) or from the starting model. **R² drops along a series are flagged** (a seeded start can drift), as is any R² < 0.9. A failed single fit keeps its start and says so.
  - **Joint refinement** when anything is shared: starts from the sequential results mapped back through the links (widths by regressing FWHM against 1/ν0; site shares averaged, scales from the totals), then `least_squares` over every spectrum at once, each weighted by its own residual RMS from the sequential pass. Errors from the joint Jacobian, propagated to every experiment's values (numerical gradient of each link), so a shared C_Q shows the same value and error in every column and a γ-scaled J the scaled error. Checked by Monte Carlo (8 noise realisations): scatter of a shared C_Q 0.0019 MHz vs reported 0.0016.
  - A width split with one field in its group is **held at width_Hz = 0** and said, since the two parts cannot be separated.
- **Fit > Multi-spectrum** (`gui/multi_fit_panel.MultiFitPanel`), last Fit section:
  - Experiments table in fitting order: **Add selected** (list order), **Add by number…** (dataset folder + "5, 302, 12-14, 2", ranges either way; opens what is not open, switches to what is), Up/Down/Remove; per row MAS (from MASR), transitions, window, x value; **x from TE (K) or time since the first (DATE, min)**.
  - Sites per nucleus: the Combined-Hamiltonian site editor (`_SiteEditor`, setup rows hidden -- the base panel now keeps `_setup_form`), a nucleus selector, **Copy sites from** another nucleus (labels, δ, widths, CSA; C_Q scaled by Q when both are quadrupolar).
  - Parameters table: Site, Parameter, Nuclei, **Scope** (combo; widths offer "per nucleus / global (Hz + ppm)"), Free, Min, Max; δ offset rows where a site is in more than one nucleus. Situation preset (Series / Isotopes / Fields / Custom -- editing a scope switches to Custom), Site amounts, Start each fit (previous / starting model), theory, orientations, baseline.
  - **Fit All** with a progress dialog and Cancel. Results: a table of every parameter across the experiments (scope in the row label), share/P_Q/CT c.o.g., summary with R² per spectrum, joint χ², width split and offsets, warnings; **Show**: any experiment's fit, or any parameter's **trend** against x (new `MplCanvas.show_parameter_trend`); right-click Copy Table / **Export CSV** / Copy Full Report.
  - Saved with **every** spectrum in the fit (`fits["multi"]`: its own curves, everyone's parameters), so each spectrum's log records the fit it was part of and its save points hold it. Selecting one brings it back **only if the panel is empty or holds the same experiments** -- it never overwrites a set being built (`_restore_multi_fit`); opening/fitting sets `_busy` so selections made on the way cannot restore anything.

### Not done / open
- **Recovery note**: this round's session was interrupted and `notebook/multi_fitting.py` was rebuilt from its compiled bytecode (docstrings verbatim); all 20 multi-fit tests pass against the rebuilt file, but review it with fresh eyes.
- Isotope links assume no isotope effect beyond a δ offset: secondary isotope effects on C_Q/J (e.g. 1H vs 2H bonded partners) and different relaxation/linewidth per isotope are not modelled -- widths are per experiment in the Isotopes preset for that reason.
- "Add selected" adds in list order (Qt does not keep click order); arbitrary order via Up/Down or typing numbers.
- Pseudo-2D rows are not experiments here (keep a slice first); a series inside one pseudo-2D stays with Fit > Isotropic's per-slice fits.
- J groups are linked across isotopes by index; the user must add them in corresponding order.
- Sharing site ratios across isotopes assumes the same isotopic distribution at every site (said in the tooltip); partially/selectively labelled samples need per-nucleus amounts.
- Opening by number uses procno 1.
- The fit blocks the window (with progress and Cancel) rather than running on a worker thread.

### Tests
`tests/test_multi_fitting.py` (11): presets; Q- and γ-scaling and offset links; a series in the given order, seeded, with trend and progress messages; a shared C_Q across a series fitted jointly; cancel; two fields and MAS rates sharing δ/C_Q/η_Q, recovering the Hz + ppm width split (150 Hz, 0.4 ppm) and a shared 2:1 site ratio with one scale held; one field holds width_Hz; 1H/2H sharing δ and J scaled by γ with propagated errors; a freed isotope offset (0.25 ppm) recovered; tables/CSV/report/plots; named errors. `tests/test_gui_multi_fit.py` (9): placement, expno parsing, opening by number in typed order with TE/DATE x values and no duplicates, a series through the GUI with trend drawn against x, two fields sharing a site, isotopes with per-nucleus sites, copying and custom scopes, stored with every spectrum and restored without overwriting a set in progress, named errors, state round trip.

Combos/checks are restored first and values twice, so a combo that re-ranges or hides a spin box does not lose its value. Each value is stored with its display text and its form label, so logs read "Larmor frequency: 130.3000 MHz". `describe_state`, `table_text`.

Every fitter's result (quadrupolar, J first-order and spin-system, CSA) encodes with nothing unsupported once the spectrum object is dropped (tested).

So the processing sidecar saves it, the log records it ("Quadrupolar fit of …" with the result table and the settings), save points hold it, Load Progress restores it, and reopening shows it.

Re-runs of the same panel within 90 s are folded into one entry (`runs`). **File ▸ Simulation History…** lists them newest first with a preview; Restore puts the inputs back, opens Simulate with the section expanded, and re-runs it (not journalled again). pNMR is restored but not re-run (an enumeration can take minutes).

## Save Progress / Load Progress and a per-spectrum processing log (2026-09-26)

User: *"have a user 'save progress' on a spectrum, and ... create a log file for each spectrum handled ... used to 'save' and 'load' progress ... stored in the same location as the data itself (for Bruker, inside the data directory) ... human readable ... The same is true for simulated data; I am unsure where best these log files should be placed."*

### What already existed (checked first)
Every processing/analysis change was *already* auto-saved to `opennmr_processing.json` + `opennmr_metadata.json` in the experiment folder and restored on reopen (`io.persistence`). Missing: any human-readable record, any history, any way back to an earlier state, and anything for simulations/derived spectra. So this builds on that state rather than defining a second one.

### Built
- **`io/history.py`** (Qt-free). Two files next to the data (same dir-vs-file rule as the sidecars): `opennmr_history.json` (the record: changes, save points with full state, restores) and `opennmr_log.txt` (generated from the JSON on every write, **never parsed back** -- a hand-edited number in a text file must not be able to change what a restore produces).
  - The tracked state is `persistence.processing_state(spectrum)` (new; exactly what the processing sidecar writes) plus mass/nucleus/pseudo-2D. A save point therefore records what a restart would restore, by construction.
  - Changes are found by **diffing** that state at each debounced sidecar save, not by instrumenting controls, so a control added later is logged without a code change (unknown keys appear under their raw name). Readable labels/units in `KEY_INFO`; `analysis_state` is flattened so each fit setting is its own line; fit/integration result texts are logged verbatim (markup stripped); combo indices are logged by name via a new `analysis_state.option_names` (log-only, never read on restore).
  - A burst of edits to the same settings within 90 s is merged into one entry (LB 0 → 10, not 0 → 1 → 10); an edit undone inside the burst leaves no entry. A setting first appearing at a blank value is not a change. Values > 20 kB (DOSY maps, per-slice fit tables) are fingerprinted in change entries, kept in full only in the state and save points.
  - Summaries list only settings that mean something (LB only with EM/GM, LP order only with LP on, baseline parameters only for the method in use, the file's own nucleus omitted); everything is still stored and restored.
  - openNMR **dataset folders** for spectra with nothing on disk: `opennmr_spectrum.npz` (data + axes, exact) + `opennmr_spectrum.json` + the usual sidecars/log. Registered as io vendor `"opennmr"`, so File ▸ Open / `io.load` reopen them. Save-point data snapshots (`opennmr_savepoints/savepoint_N.npz`) for anything that cannot be recomputed from a raw FID.
- **GUI** (`gui/progress.py` dialogs; logic on `MainWindow`: `_begin_history`, `_record_history`, `_save_progress`, `_restore_progress`, `_apply_restored_state`). File menu: **Save Progress… (Ctrl+Shift+S)**, **Load Progress… (Ctrl+Shift+L)**, **Processing Log…**.
  - Reference point = the state once the saved recipe is applied at load, with the controls' starting values filling untouched settings (`_fid_processing_control_values`, split out of `_persist_fid_processing_controls_to_metadata`), so the first LB edit logs "0 → 5 Hz" and not every other default.
  - **Opening alone writes nothing** into a data folder; the "Opened" entry is written with the first change. A state that differs on opening from the log's last record (older openNMR, copied sidecars) is logged as such.
  - Save Progress commits a phase still held only by the controls and the analysis panel first. Restore **re-reads the files with the original load kwargs (plus the saved pseudo-2D/magnitude choice) and applies the state through `_apply_loaded_processing_sidecar`** -- the reopen path -- rather than a second way of applying a recipe; non-reprocessable spectra restore from their snapshot. Restoring first keeps the current state as an "Automatic: before restoring ..." save point unless one already holds it. "Original" = re-read with no openNMR processing.
  - Simulations/derived: history kept in memory (session `info(index)["history"]`, which moves with the spectrum and survives reload/reset) with a "Created" entry listing the simulation parameters and an "As created" save point holding the data. Save Progress asks for a folder: default `<parent expno>/opennmr_derived/<name>/` for anything derived from an experiment (Session.add_derived now records `origin`), `~/Documents/openNMR/simulations/<date>_<name>/` for simulations. After saving, the spectrum becomes vendor `opennmr` with that folder and is logged like any experiment.
  - A log that cannot be written (read-only, offline cloud folder) is reported once on the status bar and in the log window, never raised mid-edit.
  - **Fixed on the way:** closing the window within the 0.8 s sidecar debounce lost the last change (and now its log entry); `closeEvent` flushes it.
- **Notebook** (`notebook/progress.py`): `processing_log`, `processing_history`, `list_save_points`, `save_point_state`, `save_progress` (a notebook simulation → dataset folder the GUI opens), `log_event` (your own lines), `load_progress`, `load_saved_spectrum`.

### Deliberately not done / open
- A notebook cannot re-apply a raw-FID experiment's saved *settings* (that is the GUI's processing chain, `_apply_loaded_processing_sidecar` and friends); `load_progress` raises `NotImplementedError` there and points to `save_point_state`. Moving that chain Qt-free would lift it.
- Notebook processing functions (`one_d`, fitting on `results` dicts) are not auto-logged; `nb.log_event` is the manual route.
- Only state that lives in `metadata.raw` is logged/restored. The panels that keep their own state outside it (Fit ▸ CSA/Quadrupolar/J-coupling/Combined, Simulate inputs, pNMR's own settings files) are not; their results are logged only if they reach `analysis_state`'s result texts.
- Phase is logged as openNMR's own correction on top of the file's recorded PHC0/PHC1 (said in the log header), matching `phase0`/`phase1`'s meaning.
- One sidecar/history per expno folder, shared across procnos -- as the existing sidecars already are.

### Tests
`tests/test_history.py` (27: diffing/wording, merging, save points, files, snapshots, dataset folders, summaries, notebook API) and `tests/test_gui_progress.py` (19: log follows edits, opening writes nothing, close flush, unwritable folder, save/restore exact data for 1D and 2D, original, across a restart, drift note, processed-only snapshots, simulations saved and reopened, dialogs).

## Tutorial notebook: quadrupolar + combined-Hamiltonian simulation and fitting; combined fitting built (2026-09-25, seventh round)

User: *"add, to the jupyter notebook, details and examples of how to use the quadrupolar simulation and fitting code, and how to combine CSA, quadrupole and/or J-coupling to simulate and also fit using the combined Hamiltonian."*

Combined-Hamiltonian **fitting did not exist yet** (the previous commit's title says "fitting"; it contains the simulator only), so it was built first, then documented.

### Built
- **`notebook/combined_fitting.py`**: `fit_combined(results, sites, vary=, fixed=, bounds=, mas_Hz=, order=, transitions=, fit_regions=, fit_baseline=, ...)` -- per-site parameters named `delta_iso, amount, fwhm, [eta], aniso, asym, [alpha, beta, gamma], C_Q, eta_Q, J1, J2, ...` (`site_parameter_names`); Euler angles fixed unless asked for; amounts started by NNLS; per-site stick spectra cached (a Jacobian column re-simulates only the site it touches; amount/FWHM changes re-simulate nothing). Returns fitted `Site`s, a parameter table with 1σ errors, derived shares (%, numbers of nuclei), P_Q and CT centre of gravity with propagated errors, quality, warnings, log. `fit_combined_multistart` (grid of starts, best χ², optional coarse screening), `print_combined_fit_report`, `plot_combined_fit` (data/fit/sites/residual), `NMRCombinedFitWorkflow`. Exported from `opennmr.notebook`. `combined_hamiltonian._site_sticks` split out of `simulate_combined` for this.
- **Tutorial** (`SCRIPT_openNMR_Tutorial_20260917.ipynb`, insertions only, executed outputs included): §3.3 quadrupolar simulation (orders compared, CT/ST components, MAS, per-orientation frequencies), §3.4 Combined Hamiltonian (Site API, physics and Euler convention, one interaction at a time static and MAS, two sites, Copy-as-Python), §4.3 quadrupolar fitting (start estimate, static and MAS, workflow on real data, what to check), §4.4 combined fitting (parameter names, vary/fixed/bounds, what a spectrum does and does not determine, the MAS-then-static route with multi-start, workflow on real data).

### Found while writing the examples (all now in the tutorial text or fixed)
- **A fast-MAS CT spectrum barely determines a CSA**: at 20 kHz the CT sidebands hold < 1 % of the intensity, and Δ = +60/η = 0.2 vs Δ = −26/η = 0 differ by 0.3 % in χ². Fit C_Q/η_Q/δiso/J/amounts from MAS, then the CSA from a static (or slow-MAS) spectrum with those fixed.
- **Static CSA+quadrupolar fits are multimodal**: of 8 starts, 5 reached Δ = 60.0 / η = 0.200 and 3 stopped at R² 0.26–0.47 -- hence `fit_combined_multistart` and the "poor fit" warning.
- The baseline-on-the-pattern warning checked only the *fitted* pattern; a fit dragged off by that baseline can move its own pattern out of the zone (R² 0.52, no warning). It now checks the starting model too.
- **Static powder defaults were too low for publication-quality lineshapes**: a 0.4 ppm-broadened CSA+quadrupolar pattern had 7.5 % powder ripple at 10946 orientations, 0.5 % at 75025 -- which costs 0.04 s. Defaults raised: static simulation 75025 (`simulate_combined`, `quadrupolar_static_spectrum`), static fitting 28657 (`fit_combined`, `fit_quadrupolar_spectrum`); MAS unchanged (already converged). GUI tooltips updated.
- `plot_combined` gained `xlims` (show the centreband when the axis also holds sidebands); site colours in `plot_combined_fit` moved clear of the fit's vermilion.

### Tests
`tests/test_combined_fitting.py` (7): parameter names; MAS recovery of C_Q, η_Q, δiso, J and the 2:1 ratio; static CSA with MAS values fixed via multi-start; vary/fixed/bounds (Euler only on request) and errors; NNLS amount start from absurd amounts; baseline warning and `fit_baseline`; report/plot/CSV/workflow. `test_combined_hamiltonian.py`: the quadrupolar-alone comparison now passes the orientation count explicitly (the default changed). Full suite, 2902 collected: all pass except the known pymatgen-only `test_gui_pnmr.py::test_a_long_label_list_is_not_dumped_into_the_log`.

## Combined Hamiltonian: CSA + quadrupolar + J on one site, static and MAS (2026-09-25, sixth round)

User: *"I want to be able to combine some/all of CSA, J-coupling and quadrupolar interactions ... I do not want separate functions for each combination, but instead would like to just 'add' an interaction to the same site ... probably a separate section, for example called 'Combined Hamiltonian'. We can start with simulating and move to fitting later."*

### Built
- **`notebook/combined_hamiltonian.py`**: `Site(nucleus, delta_iso, label, amount, fwhm, lineshape)` with `.add_csa(aniso, asym, convention, euler)`, `.add_quadrupolar(C_Q MHz, eta_Q)`, `.add_jcoupling(nuclide, n, J_Hz)` (any number), generic `.add(kind, ...)`, `.remove`, `.to_dict/.from_dict`; `simulate_combined(sites, ppm_axis, larmor_Hz|B0_T, mas_Hz, order, transitions, ...)` → total, per-site, per-transition-group spectra and a log; `site_transition_frequencies` (per orientation), `combined_axis_limits`, `combined_to_python` (notebook code that reproduces a GUI simulation), `sites_to_json/from_json`, `plot_combined`. Exported from `opennmr.notebook`.
- Physics: frequencies add (CSA first order, quadrupolar first/second/exact, heteronuclear weak J as a multiplet convolution via `combine_jcouplings`); CSA orientation in the EFG frame by ZYZ Euler angles (β, α = polar angles of δzz in the EFG frame). One engine for static and MAS (the quadrupolar simulator's gamma-COMPUTE, now factored into `simulations._mas_prepare/_mas_sticks`).
- Powder: one octant only when exact (no CSA, or CSA axes coincident with the EFG's); otherwise the full sphere, with 8× the points for static patterns (a tilted CSA+quadrupolar static pattern was 15% off at 4181 full-sphere points). Forcing the octant on a tilted CSA gives a 92% error -- the automatic check is necessary.
- **GUI, Simulate > Combined Hamiltonian** (after Quadrupolar; `gui/combined_panels.py`): shared nucleus/Larmor/regime/MAS/transitions/quadrupolar theory/orientations; a site list (Add, Duplicate, Remove); the selected site's label, δiso, amount, broadening, and its interactions -- "Add interaction ▾" (CSA, Quadrupolar, J-coupling; CSA and quadrupolar once per site, quadrupolar only for I ≥ 1), each with its own Remove; Euler angles enabled only with an EFG. Auto axis, Simulate (total on the spectrum plot, each site on the Simulation plot), Export to Open Experiments, **Copy as Python**. Seeded from the selected spectrum (nucleus, SFO1, MASR).

### Bug found and fixed (in the previous round's code)
- `quadrupolar_mas_spectrum`'s octant shortcut **averaged sideband k with −k**, on the argument that a reflected rotor axis mirrors the sideband pattern. It does not: the reflected trajectory is time-reversed, the time-reversed signal is the complex conjugate, and |a_k|² is unchanged. Harmless for quadrupolar-only patterns (each satellite pair is a mirror pair; CT sidebands are tiny) -- which is why the tests passed -- but it made CSA sideband patterns symmetric. Removed; a CSA-only MAS site now matches `finite_mas_csa_spectrum` sideband by sideband (e.g. −1: 0.330 vs 0.330, +1: 0.1454 vs 0.1455) and the test checks the asymmetry.
- Auto axis under MAS: the static range does not contain the sidebands of a CSA spun slower than its width; `combined_axis_limits(mas_Hz=...)` frames on a quick coarse MAS simulation instead.

### Tests
`tests/test_combined_hamiltonian.py` (19): each interaction alone equals its dedicated simulator (quadrupolar static/MAS, CSA static, CSA finite-MAS incl. sideband asymmetry, J multiplet); CSA+quadrupolar per-orientation frequencies vs an independent dense calculation (scipy ZYZ rotation, explicit RS sums) at four Euler sets; Euler meaning; octant only when exact (vs full-sphere references); MAS sidebands of a tilted CSA+quadrupolar crystallite vs an explicit rotor-phase average; J under MAS; several sites, amounts, CT shares; spin-1/2; Python export reproduces the result; axis framing incl. MAS sidebands; plot. `tests/test_gui_combined.py` (5): building a site by adding interactions equals the notebook call; one CSA/one EFG per site; spin-1/2 disables quadrupolar/transitions; duplicate/rename/remove and the per-site plot; Copy as Python reproduces the GUI result; seeding and refusals. Changed: the two Simulate section-order tests now include "Combined Hamiltonian".

Full suite (2895 collected, run in chunks on the VM, without `test_data/`, with pymatgen): all pass except the known pymatgen-only `test_gui_pnmr.py::test_a_long_label_list_is_not_dumped_into_the_log`.

### Not done / open
- **Fitting** with combined sites (next step, by request): the engine is already vectorised and deterministic, so `fit_combined` can follow the quadrupolar fitter's pattern (flatten each site's parameters, fixed/bounds per site and per interaction).
- Heteronuclear **dipolar** coupling (first order, orientation-dependent) would slot in as a fourth interaction the same way; homonuclear/strong coupling needs `spin_system`, not this.
- CSA–quadrupolar cross terms beyond first order are neglected (≲1e-6 of the CSA); J is isotropic only (no anisotropic J).
- The GUI's Simulate > CSA / Quadrupolar / J-coupling sections remain; they could become presets of this section.

## Quadrupolar fitting, static and MAS (2026-09-25, fifth round)

User: *"Can we now add quadrupolar (static and MAS) to the fit section? (And likewise add it to the notebook functions)"*

### Built
- **`notebook/quadrupolar_fitting.py`** (new): `fit_quadrupolar_spectrum` (one or more sites; per site δiso ppm, C_Q MHz, η_Q, FWHM ppm, amplitude, pseudo-Voigt fraction; spin from `results['nuclide']` or `I=`; Larmor from SFO1; static or MAS; `order` second/exact/first; `transitions` ct/all/st; global or per-site `fixed`/`bounds` as in the CSA fitter; `fit_baseline`), `estimate_quadrupolar_start` (C_Q from the pattern's width by matching simulations -- CT width ∝ C_Q², first-order ∝ C_Q -- and δiso from the centre of gravity less the CT isotropic shift), `evaluate_quad_fit`, `quadrupolar_derived` (P_Q and the CT centre of gravity, with errors propagated from the covariance -- checked against Monte Carlo), `print_quadrupolar_fit_report`, `NMR1dplot_with_quad_fit` (data, fit, sites, residual panel), `NMRQuadFitWorkflow` (import → start → fit → report/plot/CSV). Exported from `opennmr.notebook`.
- **GUI, Fit > Quadrupolar** (new section after CSA/Dipolar; `gui/quadrupolar_panels.py`): sites table (right-click fix / bounds, italics when fixed), Add/Remove site, Estimate from data, nucleus/Larmor/MAS rate seeded from the selected spectrum (MASR switches Regime to MAS), Transitions, Model, Broadening, Fit window, Fit the baseline too, orientations (fit/final). Results table: δiso, C_Q, η_Q, P_Q, CT c.o.g., FWHM, amplitude, Area % with 1σ; right-click Copy Table / Copy Full Report; the setup line + R²/RMSE/χ²/time + warnings above it; "Send to Simulate > Quadrupolar" fills the simulator with the fitted site and the fit's settings.
- **Simulator: octant powder sampling** (`simulations._quad_powder`, `use_symmetry=True` default for ZCW). Exact, not an approximation: the EFG's D2h symmetry (π rotations about PAS axes) plus time reversal (b → −b leaves the spectrum of H_Z + H_Q unchanged) make every static observable the same in all eight octants. Under MAS a single sign flip reverses the rotation sense, which mirrors a crystallite's sideband pattern (k → −k), so the MAS sidebands are symmetrised. Same cost, 8× the orientation density. Measured against converged references: static max error 25% → 8% (sharp CT singularities at 0.8 ppm broadening), MAS 6.2% → 0.3%, at 4181 orientations.

### Found on the way (and handled)
- **A baseline estimated on the pattern biases everything.** A broad CT whose wing reached into the outer 5% of the spectrum gave δiso −4.86 (true −5.00), C_Q 5.97 (6.00), amplitude −18%, and a good-looking R². The fit now warns when the fitted pattern has >1% of its height inside the baseline-estimation zone, or runs past the fit window, and `fit_baseline=True` (GUI: "Fit the baseline too") recovers the truth (δiso −4.998, C_Q 6.000).
- Powder ripple from too few orientations is absorbed into a larger FWHM (0.8 → 1.44 ppm at 10946 full-sphere orientations on a 6 MHz CT); the octant sampling above removed most of it.
- `diff_step=1e-4` in `curve_fit`: the default relative step (~1.5e-8) is below the powder pattern's bin-to-bin roughness.

### Tests
`tests/test_quadrupolar_fitting.py` (11) and `tests/test_gui_quadrupolar_fit.py` (4): recovery of known parameters from exact-model, finer-grid, noisy synthetic data (static CT from an estimated start, MAS CT, two overlapping sites with a fixed η_Q, 2H with the exact model), bounds and |C_Q|, integer spin refuses CT, derived-quantity errors vs Monte Carlo, report/plot/CSV/workflow, clipping and baseline warnings; GUI seeding (nucleus, SFO1, MASR), Estimate, Fit, results table, fixed parameter, Send to Simulate, refusals. Changed: `test_main_window_fitting_tab_has_three_collapsible_sections` now expects "Quadrupolar" last.

### Not done / open
- Fitting several spectra together (e.g. two fields -- the standard way to separate δiso from C_Q, which the report points at when they are >95% correlated) is not built; nor a CSA + quadrupolar model, nor pulse-excitation effects on relative CT/ST intensities.
- The GUI fit blocks while it runs (two MAS sites ≈ 15 s); CSA's does too. Exact MAS fits are slow (seconds per evaluation) -- fit second order, then compare with Simulate's "Compare orders".
- The sites table is not updated with the fitted values (as in CSA); Send to Simulate carries the first site only.

## Quadrupolar simulator rebuilt: static + fast MAS, first/second order/exact, CT and/or STs (2026-09-25, fourth round)

User: replace the quadrupolar functions in `notebook/simulations.py` with the static simulator from `SCRIPT_Quad_Simulator_V2_20260925.ipynb` (exact / first- / second-order, CT/ST labels), and remake the MAS part, which took ~40 s for 10 crystallites. Must be able to see first- and second-order effects, and to simulate CT only or CTs and STs together.

### Why the notebook's MAS was slow (and also wrong)
- **Slow**: a Python loop over 4096 rotor phases per crystallite, and every step called `find_isotope_info` twice (a pandas DataFrame filter), rebuilt the spin operators with Python loops, built the rotated EFG and ran `eigh` -- ~1 ms of overhead per step, ~4 s per crystallite. Nothing about the quadrupole makes it harder than CSA: in high field every frequency is a closed-form function of the B0 direction in the PAS (rank 2 at first order; three rotation invariants at second order), a Fourier series in the rotor phase with at most 4 harmonics.
- **Wrong**: it subtracted each crystallite's mean frequency, which *removes the MAS CT lineshape and the isotropic quadrupolar shift* (both live in that mean); it FFT'd one rotor period, so the axis only had points at multiples of the spinning rate; `abs()` of the summed FID mixed in dispersive signal (the gamma-averaged intensity is |a_k|^2 per crystallite); the broadening kernel was defined on that coarse grid.

### Built (`notebook/simulations.py`, QUADRUPOLAR NMR section -- replaces every previous quadrupolar function)
- `quadrupolar_static_spectrum`, `quadrupolar_mas_spectrum`, `quadrupolar_spectrum` (dispatch on `mas_Hz`), `quadrupolar_order_comparison` (first/second/exact + difference spectra), `quadrupolar_transition_frequencies` (per orientation), `quadrupolar_transition_table`, `quadrupolar_axis_limits`, `quadrupolar_ct_isotropic_shift_Hz`, `quadrupolar_nu_Q`, `larmor_frequency_Hz`. `order='first'|'second'|'exact'`; `transitions='ct'|'st'|'all'|'ST1'|[...]`; `delta_iso`; results carry `components` per transition group and a one-line `log`.
- Intensities are normalised so all 2I transitions sum to 1: a CT-only spectrum integrates to the CT's true share (9/35 for I = 5/2).
- MAS: gamma-COMPUTE. 16 rotor-phase samples (exact for perturbative orders; 32 for exact), phase integrated in the Fourier domain, sidebands |a_k|^2 at c0 + k nu_r; n_time chosen from the largest excursion so no sideband aliases (raises past `max_n_time`). Exact MAS = batched `eigh` at each sampled rotor phase (adiabatic; rotor-averaged intensities).
- Speed (VM, 2 cores): MAS CT 4181 crystallites second order 0.04 s, exact 0.55 s; CT+STs ~0.5 s (second) / 1.2 s (exact). Static 17711 orientations: <0.01 s perturbative, 0.09 s exact.
- `notebook/plotting.py`: `plot_quadrupolar_orders` -- first/second/exact overlaid (Okabe-Ito + distinct dashes), difference panel below; `scale='each'|'shared'`; `figure=` to draw into the GUI's plot.
- GUI, Simulations > Quadrupolar: Regime (Static / MAS) + MAS rate, Transitions (CT + satellites / CT only / satellites only), Method (Exact / Second-order / First-order), δiso, "Compare orders" (draws `plot_quadrupolar_orders` on the Simulation plot; the exported spectrum is still the chosen method's), Auto axis (framed at Simulate time; typing a limit turns it off). The result line reports ν_Q, time taken and the CT isotropic quadrupolar shift; the full log is its tooltip and in the exported spectrum's metadata.

### Validation (`tests/test_quadrupolar_simulation.py`, 22 tests; 4 new GUI tests in `test_gui.py`)
- Per-orientation first/second/exact against a dense lab-frame reference (rotated EFG, explicit Rayleigh-Schroedinger sums): agree to <1e-4 Hz, I = 1, 3/2, 5/2, 7/2. Also checked against the notebook's own functions: <1e-6 Hz.
- Second - exact below the third-order scale; CT powder mean = the textbook isotropic shift; eta = 0 static CT edges at +A and -16A/9; 2H Pake horns at +-3C_Q/8; intensity shares.
- MAS sideband intensities against an explicit average over starting rotor phases of the time signal integrated step by step (agree to ~1e-7 relative when converged); MAS CT centre of gravity = delta_iso + isotropic shift; MAS second vs exact.

### Removed
`static_quadrupolar_spectrum`, `_exact`, `_decomposed`, `quadrupolar_transitions(_exact)`, `quadrupolar_transition_decomposition`, `quadrupolar_second_order_map`, `quadrupolar_hamiltonian`, `_quad_operators`, `mas_quadrupolar_fid`, `rotation_matrix`, `efg_orientation`, `_transverse_basis`. Only `static_quadrupolar_spectrum_exact` was exported from `opennmr.notebook`; nothing else in `src/` or the tutorial notebooks used them.

### Not done / open
- The notebook's "second-order intensities" (from first-order-corrected states) were not carried over: perturbative orders use Zeeman intensities, 'exact' uses the true eigenvectors. The difference is O(C_Q/nu0).
- GUI MAS is magic-angle only (`rotor_angle` is available in the notebook function). No CSA + quadrupolar combination, no finite pulse / excitation effects (CT-selective vs non-selective intensities), no quadrupolar *fitting* yet -- the fast engine makes a `curve_fit` over C_Q, eta_Q, delta_iso practical.
- ZCW with stick binning leaves small "powder ripples" at low broadening; raise Orientations or FWHM.
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure (fails on HEAD too, only when pymatgen is installed): `test_gui_pnmr.py::test_a_long_label_list_is_not_dumped_into_the_log`.


## Fix: dragging a 1D onto a 2D's projection did nothing (2026-09-25, third round)

User: *"The drag and drop external projection does not seem to work... I cannot drag the 1-d into the projection on F1 or F2; all that happens is that the 1-d spectrum I want to put on the projection appears in the Spectrum window."*

### What was wrong
`spectrum_list` was a plain `QListWidget`, which selects a row on mouse **press**, and selecting a row shows it on the Spectrum canvas. Pressing on the 1D to start dragging it therefore swapped the 2D out for the 1D *before* the drag left the list. By the time it reached the plot there was no contour, and the canvas's drop filter (correctly) refused it. The first round's tests fed the drop straight to the canvas and never started a drag from the list, so they could not see this.

### Fixed
`MainWindow._ExperimentSourceList` replaces it.
- A plain left press on a row is held back. Moving past `startDragDistance` starts a drag of that row (or of the whole selection, if the row is part of it), with selection and plot untouched. Releasing without moving replays the press as an ordinary click.
- Ctrl/Shift presses, other buttons and the keyboard go straight to Qt.
- The drag itself is `_start_drag(mime)`, a seam, because a real `QDrag` runs its own event loop, which a headless test cannot finish.
- Dragging into Compare no longer changes the plot either.

Regression test `test_dragging_a_1d_out_of_open_experiments_leaves_the_2d_on_screen` drives real mouse events on the list's viewport, then drops the payload the list produced. It fails on the old `QListWidget` with exactly the reported symptom (the canvas showing the 1D after the press). There are also tests that a plain click still selects and shows, and that Ctrl-click still extends the selection at once.

## Projection style by right-clicking the strip; separate F2/F1 axis labels (2026-09-25, second round)

User: *"Can we control the plot style of the projections by right clicking the projection specifically? Also, can we add something where, for 2-d spectra, we can edit the labels of both axes separately? e.g., if someone wanted to keep the name of the F2 axis but change F1."*

### What already existed
Projections were always drawn in black (crimson if external), with one `projection_size` for both strips and no way to set either from the GUI. Plot Style's "Custom label" is one template for *every* chemical-shift axis on a canvas, so it could not change F1 without changing F2. The notebook's `NMR2Dplotter` already takes `xlabel`/`ylabel` separately, so the notebook side of the labels needed nothing.

### Built
- **`projection_style={"f1": {...}, "f2": {...}}`** on `plotting.twod.plot_2d_contour` *and* the notebook's `NMR2Dplotter`: `color`, `linewidth`, `linestyle`, `size` (inches, per strip) and `visible`. Both validate through one function, `plotting.twod.projection_line_kwargs`; a misspelt key such as `colour` raises rather than doing nothing. A set colour overrides the external projection's crimson.
- **Right-clicking a strip** (the canvas records `event.inaxes` on every right-press, as `_last_right_click_axes`) puts *"F1 (left)/F2 (top) Projection Style…"* and *"Hide … Projection"* at the top of the menu.
  - The dialog (`_ProjectionStyleDialog`) has colour (with Default), line width, line style, strip size, show, "Apply to both projections" and Restore Defaults. Changes preview live, and Cancel restores the earlier settings.
  - The style is per canvas, like the rest of Plot Style, so it carries over to the next 2D. A hidden strip gets *"Show F1/F2 Projection"* on the contour's menu, and dropping a 1D onto a hidden strip shows it again.
  - API: `set_projection_style` / `projection_style` / `reset_projection_style`.
- **Edit Axis Labels (F2 / F1)…** on the contour's right-click menu (`_AxisLabelsDialog`): one box per axis, where blank means automatic.
  - An untouched axis stays automatic (no override stored), so it keeps following Plot Style's label style.
  - Each box has a preview rendered by matplotlib itself. A label that cannot be drawn disables OK and shows why.
  - `set_axis_label_override` refuses such a label too (`_render_label`). **An unknown mathtext command raises only at draw time, and would otherwise break the whole canvas.**
  - Labels are stored per 2D, keyed like the external projections, and forgotten when the 2D is removed. They survive redraws, full-resolution export and reselection.
  - `{nuc}`/`{mass}`/`{element}`/`{unit}` are filled in *for that axis* by plain replacement, not `str.format`, which would choke on the braces in mathtext (`$^{13}$C`).
  - A label without `{unit}` is shown only in the unit it was typed in; in any other unit the axis falls back to the automatic label. This stops a typed "(ppm)" staying on an axis switched to Hz. Pseudo-2D: F1 is not editable (it is a slice number).
- Tests: `tests/test_projection_style_and_labels.py` (18). The notebook's external-projection check is now exercised through a real `NMR2Dplotter` call (`test_two_d._make_dataset`), not by source inspection.

### Tried and rejected
- Pre-filling the label boxes with the automatic label: its raw text is `$\mathregular{...}$`, which is unreadable. Replaced by blank plus the rendered preview and a "Start from automatic" button.
- Patching `QMenu.exec` in a test hangs the suite (PySide opens the real menu). Use `MplCanvas._exec_context_menu`, the seam that already exists for this.

### Not done / open
- Projection style is not part of Plot Style's *Apply to all plots* / *Save as default*.
- The Compare tile's 2D panels and overlays do not use per-2D labels or projection style.

## Drag a 1D onto a 2D as an external projection (2026-09-25)

User: *"When a 2-d dataset is loaded, can we add something so that a user can drag and drop an open 1-d spectrum as an external projection? Obvs there should be a warning about whether it's the same nucleus along the dimension where they are dragging and dropping."*

### What already existed
The notebook's `NMR2Dplotter` already took `f1_external_projection`/`f2_external_projection` (an `NMR1dimport` dict or a Bruker path), cropped to the displayed range, drawn in crimson. It checked nothing about the nucleus. The GUI draws through `plotting.twod.plot_2d_contour`, which had no external projections at all.

### Built
- **One check, shared by notebook and GUI**: `notebook.two_d.check_external_projection(dataset, projection, dimension)` (exported from `opennmr.notebook`). It accepts an `NMRSpectrum` or the notebook's dicts on either side. It returns `allowed` (False for a pseudo-2D's F1, or no ppm overlap), `nucleus_match` (True/False/None when either nucleus is unrecorded), `coverage`, `problems` (ask about these) and `notes` (just report). Nuclei are compared through `canonical_nucleus`, which reads `13C`/`C13`/`<13C>`/`Proton`/`Carbon13`/`off`. A homonuclear 2D's F1 takes the direct nucleus.
  - `NMR2Dplotter` now raises a `UserWarning` when an external projection's nucleus does not match. It still draws, since a notebook has no dialog. A path source is not imported just to check it.
- **Drawing**: `plot_2d_contour(f1_external=, f2_external=, external_projection_color='crimson')` takes a 1D `NMRSpectrum`, an `NMR1dimport` dict or an `(x, y)` pair. The trace is cropped to the displayed range *before* its intensity limits are set, so a solvent line outside the 2D cannot set the scale. The lower limit is `min - 2% of span`, not the computed projection's `min*0.9`, which sits above a trace that dips below zero. F1 keeps the computed one's orientation (descending xlim). A pseudo-2D's F1 is refused. Lines carry `gid="external_projection_f1/f2"`.
- **GUI drop**: the plot accepts drags from Open experiments (the same `application/x-qabstractitemmodeldatalist` payload the Compare list takes, decoded by the now-shared `canvas._rows_from_list_drag`). Drop handling is an event filter on the `FigureCanvasQTAgg`. File drops are ignored there, so they still reach the main window's folder drop. While dragging, the strip under the cursor is tinted.
  - Released over the top/left strip, that strip is the target. Released over the contour, the nuclei decide when exactly one dimension matches; otherwise it asks F2 / F1 / Both (homonuclear, or no nucleus recorded).
  - `MainWindow._confirm_external_projection`: a mismatch or an unconfirmable nucleus asks first (`QMessageBox.question`, default **No**). If the 1D matches the *other* axis, the message says to drop it on that strip. Anything that cannot be drawn is refused with a warning. Partial coverage goes to the status line.
  - The signal is emitted via `QTimer.singleShot(0, ...)`, outside Qt's drag loop, because a modal dialog inside a drop is unreliable on Windows.
- **Canvas state** (`MplCanvas.set_external_projection` / `clear_external_projection` / `external_projection` / `external_projections_for` / `prune_external_projections`): kept per 2D, keyed by `id()` with the 2D held alongside, so a recycled id cannot leak.
  - The projections survive level scrolls, reprocessing, unit changes, full-resolution export and switching to another spectrum and back.
  - The 1D is held by reference, so re-phasing it shows at the next redraw.
  - Removing either spectrum from Open experiments (or Clear All) drops the projection.
  - Right-click > *Remove External F2/F1 Projection (label)*.
  - The strip's intensity zoom is reset when its content changes (`_redraw_contour(fresh_projections=...)`).
- **Units**: in Hz/kHz/mm the 1D's ppm is mapped through the *2D's own* axis (linear fit ppm → unit), not the 1D's Hz axis. A 1D recorded at another field has a different Hz axis for the same shifts. Tested with a 600 MHz 1D on a 400 MHz 2D.
- **Processing report**: for a 2D showing one, File > Processing Report adds "The F2 (top) projection shown is not computed from this 2D: it is the separately acquired 1D spectrum …", so a figure made this way says so.
- Tests: `tests/test_external_projection.py` (33).
  - Qt 6 does not deliver a synthetic `QDropEvent` through `sendEvent` without a real drag, so the tests call `canvas.eventFilter(canvas.canvas, event)` directly. That is the code path a real drop runs.

### Not done / open
- Only the first 1D of a multi-row drag is used (said in the status line). Several 1Ds on one strip (a stacked projection) was not asked for.
- The external trace is crimson, as in the notebook. It may want to follow the Plot Style trace colour for figures; not decided.
- No chemical-shift referencing check between the 1D and the 2D beyond ppm overlap. A 1D referenced differently will simply sit offset.

## 2D spectra in Compare: overlay (up to 6), side by side, insets (2026-09-24, ninth round)

User: *"I have, in the notebook, something that can, for 2-d datasets: Overlay multiple 2-d spectra on top of each other; Plot 2-d spectra side-by-side; Add insets to 2-d spectra. In the "Compare" tab, can we add these 2-d functions in?"* Chosen when asked: insets made by **zooming, then "Add inset"** (then editable); overlay limit **raised to 6** (notebook too).

### What already existed
Compare already overlaid 2-3 genuine 2Ds automatically (`plotting.twod.overlay_plot`, the GUI port of `NMR2D_overlay_plot`). `plotting.twod.multi_plot` (port of `NMR2D_multi_plot`) existed but was never wired in, and could only make its own figure. The port had no insets at all.

### Built
- `plotting/twod.py`: `draw_insets` (+ `inset_bounds`, `crop_2d`, `MAX_OVERLAY_SPECTRA = 6`); `insets=` on `plot_2d_contour` and `overlay_plot`; `multi_plot(fig=...)` draws into an existing figure (GUI canvas) without touching global style/size.
  - An inset is drawn from **its region at full resolution** (the parent is downsampled for speed, which a zoom would expose) with **levels from the whole spectrum**, so a contour means the same intensity in inset and parent; an inset may lower its own floor. F1/F2 labels face into the plot (a right-corner inset puts F1 labels left; a lower-corner inset puts F2 labels on top) so they never print over the parent's labels. Box + connectors via `indicate_inset_zoom`.
  - Not the notebook's recursion into the full plotter: that builds an `AxesDivider` on the inset, which replaces the inset's placement (the notebook refuses projections in insets for this reason).
- `canvas.show_2d_overlay(..., insets, factor, clevels)`, new `canvas.show_2d_panels(spectra, labels, layout, projections, link_axes, insets, ...)`, `canvas.zoomed_2d_region()`. Linked panels use limit callbacks, **not** `sharex`: each panel inverts its own axes, and inverting a shared axis once per panel flips it back and forth.
- `gui/compare_2d.py`: `Compare2DControls` (the "2D spectra" box in Compare, shown when a 2D is checked): Layout (Overlay / Side by side: row, column, grid), Link zoom, Projections, lowest contour %, levels; Insets list + editor (panel or all, F2/F1 range, corner, size, lowest contour, connector).
- `MainWindow._refresh_compare_2d` replaces `_refresh_compare_2d_overlay`: any all-2D selection (including a single 2D, so one spectrum can get an inset). ## CPMG echo co-addition in Advanced Processing (2026-09-24, eighth round)

User: *"Can we now add in the CPMG Skyline projection processing to "Advanced Processing" (making the VOCS and CPMG Skyline as separate collapsable sections)"* -- clarified: wire in the notebook's existing `CPMGprocess` (co-add the echoes of a raw Bruker echo train, apodise, zero-fill, FT). There is no skyline step in it; a per-echo 2D + skyline projection, or a skyline combination of several spectra, was offered and not chosen.

### Built
- Adv. Proc. is now two `CollapsibleSection`s: **VOCS** (unchanged content) and **CPMG** (`gui/cpmg_panel.py`, `CpmgProcessingPanel`, `MainWindow.cpmg_panel`). The panel follows the Open experiments selection; selecting a CPMG *result* keeps the raw experiment as the source, so settings can be tweaked and re-run.
  - Pulse-programme indices (d6 echo length, d3 blanking, cnst20, l22 echo count by default) as spin boxes.
  - Echo split: first point auto (+offset) or manual, safety, skip first N echoes, echoes to co-add. *Check echo split* reports the resolved timings/period and draws |FID| with every echo window shaded (alternating shades; co-added blue, left-out grey; zoomable), before anything is processed.
  - Processing: apodisation (zeroed edges, shape, alpha), zero-fill (Auto or points), magnitude or phase-sensitive (then phase with the normal Phase controls). Result added to Open experiments as `CPMG <expno>`; a log line records everything used.
- Notebook (`notebook/one_d.py`, exported): `cpmg_echo_layout` (the split, without processing -- what the preview uses and what `CPMGprocess` now calls), `cpmg_to_spectrum` (result -> `NMRSpectrum`, with `acqus` carried so VOCS/named constants work on it, and `raw["cpmg"]` recording the split).

### Fixed in `CPMGprocess` on the way (behaviour changes -- flagged to the user)
1. **ppm axis referencing.** Was `(offset + O1) / SFO1`; now `(offset + O1 - SR) / SF` with `SF` from `pdata/<procno>/procs` (else BF1) -- the same as `io.bruker`. The old form was low by the fraction O1/BF1 (1.1 ppm at 1120 ppm for a 100 kHz offset at 100 MHz) and ignored a TopSpin SR. Sign convention checked against `io.bruker.read_1d` on the same synthetic acqus: both put the line at the same ppm.
2. **Fractional echo period.** Echo windows were cut at multiples of `int(period)`, so a 53.4-point period drifted 0.4 point per echo (80 points by echo 200); measured on a synthetic 200-echo train the co-added echo lost ~10x in amplitude. Each echo now starts at `rint(k * period_exact)`; identical when the period is a whole number of points.
3. **`num_echoes_added` counts from `cutout`**, as its docstring always said (the code used it as the stop index: `cutout=2, num_echoes_added=200` co-added 198). Clamped to the echoes available; `cutout >= echoes` raises.
4. `trim` (blanking - safety) clamped at 0 -- a large safety made a negative slice index.
Unchanged: auto first point (first non-zero + offset), no digital-filter removal, apodisation window, zero-fill rule.

### Not done
- A per-echo 2D (echo number x frequency) with a skyline projection; a skyline (point-wise max) combination of several CPMG pieces beside VOCS Sum. Both straightforward on top of `cpmg_echo_layout` if wanted.
- No real CPMG dataset was available to check against; everything is on synthetic trains built to the function's own model.

### Tests
`tests/test_cpmg.py` (12): peak position vs `io.bruker` reader (plain, 100 kHz offset, with SR), fractional period (no drift, within half a point), whole period unchanged, echoes-added semantics, layout errors explained, result as spectrum (acqus carried, magnitude/phase, VOCS works); GUI: two sections, end-to-end process + re-process from the result, refusal without a source, a bad index shown not raised.


## VOCS on a column extracted from a 2D (2026-09-24, seventh round)

User: *"If I have a 2-d experiment such as a J-HMQC, and I want to extract a column corresponding to a peak at a fixed F2 ... store that column for processing. If I then wanted to account for the finite pulse for the F1 dimension, I should be able to use the VOCS section. However, because this is an extracted slice, I end up with the error 'This spectrum has no recorded acquisition parameters, so P1 cannot be looked up ...'"* -- and a pointer to the notebook workaround (`NMR1dimport(..., heteronuclear_2d_slice=True)`: axis from `acqu2s`, pulse lengths from `acqus`).

### What was wrong
`processing.slicing.get_trace` built the trace's metadata with `raw={"slice": ...}` only, so every acquisition table of the 2D was dropped and `acquisition_constants(trace)` was empty. Anything that asks for a parameter by name (VOCS pulse, fit-equation constants, MASR) failed on any kept slice, not just VOCS.

### Built
- `get_trace` copies the acquisition tables (`acqus`, `acqu2s`, `acqu3s`, X-Pulse `exp_params`/`params`) onto the trace, and records `slice["dimension"]` (`"F1"` for a column). Processing tables (`procs`/`proc2s`) are deliberately not carried -- they describe the 2D's processing. This is the notebook workaround's logic: the trace's own axis is already the F1 axis (nucleus/SFO1 from the indirect dimension), and pulse lengths come from `acqus`, where Bruker keeps the whole `P` array for all channels.
- VOCS accepts a pulse length as a number (`2.5`, `"2.5 us"`, `"2.5 µs"`) as well as a parameter name -- the fallback for spectra that genuinely have no table (arithmetic results, readers that keep none); the no-table error now says so. `processing.vocs.pulse_length_us` exposes the resolution.
- GUI: after Apply VOCS the status bar says what was used ("VOCS applied: P3 = 4 µs, ν1 = 62.5 kHz, on the 13C (F1 trace) axis"), so a pulse on the wrong channel is visible. The pulse field's tooltip notes that an F1 column needs the F1 channel's pulse (usually not P1).

### Caveats
- For a column, `acquisition_constants` also returns F2 scalars such as `td`/`sw` from `acqus` (the acquisition table is the 2D's, not the trace's). Nothing uses those for a trace today.
- The VOCS profile is centred on the middle of the trace's axis, taken as the carrier -- true for a full TopSpin F1 (and F2) window; not for a trace cut with `window=` (the GUI never does).

### Tests
`tests/test_vocs_slices.py` (4): a column carries the tables (and not procs), VOCS on an F1 column uses the F1 Hz axis and P3, numeric pulse lengths (and the errors), and the GUI path (keep a column, Apply VOCS with P3, no error, summary message).

I think having something that can also act as a title for other formats (non-Bruker) would also be good."* Chosen when asked: edits to a Bruker title **write back to `pdata/<procno>/title`** (not a sidecar), and a notes box under the list (rows get the first line as a tooltip, not in their names).

### Not done / caveats
- A slice kept as its own spectrum is registered as `derived` (`Session.add_derived`), so its notes are session-only and never touch the parent's title. (Corrected in the seventh round; the first write-up of this round said the opposite.)
- A title that was pure ASCII as acquired is treated as UTF-8; a non-ASCII character typed into it is written as UTF-8, which Windows TopSpin may display as two characters. Could be decided from the TopSpin install path recorded in `acqus` if it matters.
