### Tests
`tests/test_experiment_notes.py` (16): title read/CRLF/Latin-1, backup-once and encoding kept, no backup without an original, missing procno refused, per-procno titles; notebook round trips for Bruker, sidecar (keeps other keys, empty edit is kept, survives `save_metadata_sidecar`), Varian `text` default untouched, session-only notes; GUI: shows/saves on selection switch and idle timer, flushes on remove/clear, failed save reported, box lives inside Open experiments.

In reality, I will have any integer."* (3) *"Is it possible to pre-process F1 in the case of bruker-detected 2-d data? Having to re-process every time is quite inconvenient"* -- clarified: every *new* genuine 2D opened as pseudo-2D and had to be switched with Process Indirect Dimension (a reopened one already remembered).

### Built

1. `MainWindow.SCAN_LIMIT = 10_000` (was a silent `max_matches=500`). A scan that reaches it now says so: an information box in Open Folder, and the Data browser's status line.
2. Change proc number: `QInputDialog.getInt(..., 1, 2_147_483_647)` (was 1..999).
3. **Measured first** on a real 43-experiment folder (`800_NB_MHz_Lyon/2p5mm_HX_2H_23Na_113Cd_Na2CdFeCN6_D2O_150126A_VT_20260223`), reading parameter files only: all **7 EXSYs** (`exsy_echo3.enb`, FnMODE 5, F1 1H/2H, no list) have `proc2s FT_mod = 4` and `2rr 2ri 2ir 2ii`; all **36 series** (`satrec2Decho3`, `hahnecho2D`, `hahnecho4`; F1 off, 34 with a vdlist) have `FT_mod = 0` and `2rr 2ii` (two unprocessed). ## Isotope-resolved coupling groups, strong coupling, and the isotope table's spins (2026-09-24, fourth round)

User: *"add the coupling group in, please, as well as strong coupling (higher order) effects"* -- i.e. a coupling group covering every magnetic isotope of the partner element (last round's caveat), and exact higher-order spectra.

### Found on the way: 24 wrong nuclear spins in the isotope tables

Checking 199Hg satellites showed **199Hg with I = 3/2 (it is 1/2)**. Compared every row of both copies of the table (`notebook/utils._GAMMA_TABLE` and `core/registry._GAMMA_TABLE`) against the IAEA nuclear-moments spins as tabulated at https://www.kherb.io/docs/nmr_table.csv: **24 spins were wrong, one contiguous block 161Dy ... 209Bi** (a shifted column): e.g. 183W 5/2 (is 1/2), 187Os 3/2 (1/2), 199Hg 3/2 (1/2), 203Tl 3/2 (1/2), **205Tl 4 (1/2)**, 207Pb 3/2 (1/2), 209Bi 7/2 (9/2), 171Yb 3/2 (1/2), 177Hf 1/2 (7/2)... All corrected in both copies; every other row already matched. Anything using those nuclei's spins -- first-order multiplets/satellites (a 199Hg or 207Pb partner drew a quartet, not a doublet), `find_spin`, `quadrupolar_nuclides` -- was wrong before. `tests/test_spin_system.py::test_every_tabulated_spin_is_right` pins the whole column against the reference, with the source. **Gyromagnetic ratios were not changed**: the heavy-element values differ from the IAEA-moment-derived ones by up to ~1.5% (e.g. 207Pb 8.8816 vs 9.0038 MHz/T), which is a reference-convention difference (IUPAC frequency ratios vs bare-nucleus moments), not a transcription error -- worth a deliberate decision on which convention the table should follow.

### Built

- **All isotopes of a partner element** (`simulations.jcoupling_group_pattern(..., all_isotopes=True)`, `element_isotopes()`): each of the n positions independently holds one isotope at natural abundance; J is to the named isotope and the others' Js are scaled by gamma ratio; spin-0 remainder gives the centre line. n-fold convolution of the single-position pattern, so it equals the old behaviour exactly when only one isotope is magnetic (tested). E.g. 19F of BF4-: the 11B quartet (80.1%) plus the 10B 1:1:1:1:1:1:1 septet at J x 0.335 (19.9%). Carried through `jcoupling_fitting` (`all_isotopes` in the topology; one J fitted). GUI: an **All isotopes** tick per coupling group (refused together with an abundance override); the pattern line lists the isotopes. Not modelled: isotope shifts, and quadrupolar relaxation collapsing couplings to Cl/Br/14N.
- **Strong coupling: `notebook/spin_system.py`** (exported from `opennmr.notebook`). Explicit spins (label, nuclide, shift, `n` magnetically equivalent copies) and J between them. Exact Hamiltonian -- full J I.I between like nuclei, J IzIz between unlike -- diagonalised per block of conserved total m per nuclide (10 spin-1/2: largest block 252; 12: 924; refused above `MAX_BLOCK_DIM` = 3500). Any spin I. Transitions of the observed nuclide, intensities normalised so each observed spin sums to 1.
  - Verified three independent ways: the closed-form AB quartet (positions and roofing), the weak-coupling limit against the first-order code, and a brute-force full-Hilbert-space Kronecker-product diagonalisation written in the test (ABX with a negative J, A2B3, a spin-1 2H plus an equivalent 19F2 pair, a strongly coupled 19F pair seen from 1H) -- agreement to ~1e-14.
  - `spin_system_spectrum` (exact analytic lines; lines within fwhm/1000 drawn as one, lines < 1e-7 of the tallest dropped -- a 12-spin system has ~10^6 transitions), `coupling_strengths` (|dnu/J| per like-nucleus pair).
  - `fit_spin_system_spectrum`: shifts, Js (any sign), shared linewidth, height, **and the baseline offset** (see below). A shift that cannot affect the observed spectrum (a spin of another nucleus with no like-nucleus partner, e.g. the 31P of an ABX) is held and reported, instead of wandering (it went to 238 ppm unheld). Iteration budget counts the finite-difference Jacobian (`curve_fit`'s own `maxfev` does not -- a wandering start could run ~10 min); tolerances 1e-12.
  - **`equivalent_solutions`: the ABX ambiguity.** Measured: fitting an ABX observed on AB converged to a *different* parameter set (dnu 7.5 instead of 8.0 Hz, J_AX/J_BX 12.5/-3.5 instead of 12.0/-3.0) that reproduces the 1H spectrum to 6e-6 of the peak height -- only the X (31P) intensities differ. Each X state gives an AB quartet fixing only |dnu_AB +/- dJ/2|, so exchanging dnu_AB with dJ/2 (keeping nu_A+nu_B, J_AX+J_BX, J_AB) is the other solution. The search refits from that exchange for every observed pair sharing an unobserved partner, keeps solutions within 2% RMS of the best, and merges solutions differing only by flipping the signs of all Js to one partner (unmeasurable). Sign-flip restarts were tried first and rejected: slow (minutes) and they only found that trivial symmetry.
- **GUI** (`gui/jcoupling_panels.py`): both J-coupling panels have a **model selector** -- "First order: sites and coupling groups" / "Spin system: exact, with strong coupling". `SpinSystemEditor`: spins table + symmetric J matrix (upper triangle edited, lower mirrored), live readout of |dnu/J| per like pair (strong < 3, intermediate < 10) and largest block; right-click fix/bounds on shifts and Js when fitting. Simulate: linewidth (Hz); results say which pairs are strongly coupled ("a first-order simulation would be visibly wrong here"); notebook code; export. Fit: linewidth start, "Look for other solutions that fit equally well" (default on) -> a **Solution** selector when there are several, with the explanation; R^2 < 0.98 warning; Use fitted values as start; Open in Simulate (reproduces the fit).

### Noted, not changed

- The first-order fitter (`jcoupling_fitting`, as the CSA fitter) estimates the baseline once and holds it. Lorentzian tails raise that estimate inside a multiplet's window (0.3% of the height in the ABX test), and J bends slightly to compensate (8e-4 Hz there). The spin-system fitter fits the offset instead; the same change in `fit_jcoupling_spectrum` would be one line if wanted.
- Large spin systems are slow to *draw* (exact lines at every point: ~9 s for 10 spins, ~25 s for 12 on 20k points); fitting is practical to ~8 spins.

### Tests

`tests/test_spin_system.py` (21, incl. the spin-table check for both tables), `tests/test_gui_jcoupling.py` now 28.


## J-coupling in Simulate and Fit (2026-09-24, third round)

User: wire Euan's J-coupling simulator (`notebook/simulations.py`) and fitter (`notebook/jcoupling_fitting.py`) into the GUI -- J-coupling at the **top of Simulate**, and **between Integration and CSA/Dipolar** in Fit.

### Checked first, and what was wrong

Fitted an exact analytic Lorentzian triplet on a realistic 1H axis (32768 points, 0.171 Hz/point, descending):

1. **Every fitted centre was off by exactly one data point (-0.171 Hz) whenever the axis had an even number of points** -- i.e. all real (2^n) data. Cause: `simulations.lorentzian_broadening` built an even-length kernel peaked at index n//2, and `fftconvolve(mode="same")` centres at (n-1)//2. Odd-length axes were fine (+0.0005 Hz). **This also affected every Lorentzian (and pseudo-Voigt) CSA simulation/fit** on an even axis (the CSA default is 4096 points). Fixed: the kernel is always odd-length. Test: `test_broadening_keeps_a_line_where_it_is`.
2. **Linewidths came out 2-3% narrow**, varying with where lines fell between points: sticks were shared between the two nearest grid points before convolving, which widens each line by up to a point spacing. J itself was fine (+/-0.0004 Hz).
3. **A site's fitted amplitude meant different things on different axes**: each site's shape was divided by its maximum *on the axis it was evaluated on*. The fit used the whole axis, `print_jcoupling_fit_report` the fit region only, so a report's components/integrals could describe a different model from the one fitted.

Fix for 2 and 3: `simulations.multiplet_lineshape` -- exact closed-form lines at each stick's own position, evaluated at any points (no grid). `jcoupled_spectrum`/`multi_site_jcoupled_spectrum` use it by default (`method="analytic"`; `method="grid"` keeps the old path). `jcoupling_site_lineshape` uses it and scales each site to height 1 **at its tallest line position** (axis-independent: "amplitude" = the multiplet's height there, including neighbouring lines' tails -- not always the curve's maximum when lines overlap). The fit now evaluates the model on the fitted points only (faster; valid for disjoint windows). After: centre and J within 1e-4 Hz, linewidth within 1e-4 Hz, on odd and even axes.

Also found, **not changed** (other callers depend on it): `notebook/bridge.results_from_spectrum` substitutes **SFO1 = 1.0 MHz** when a spectrum has none, which would silently mis-scale any Hz<->ppm conversion downstream. The J-coupling panel reads SFO1 from the spectrum's metadata itself and refuses to fit without it. Worth making the bridge raise, or return None, and fixing its callers.

### Built

- **`gui/jcoupling_panels.py`**: `JCouplingSitesEditor` (sites table -- label, shift ppm, FWHM **in Hz**, plus intensity when simulating -- and, below, the selected site's coupling groups: partner, n, J Hz, abundance (blank = natural), optional bond label; a live line naming the pattern, e.g. "dq (J(P) = 140.0 Hz, J(H) = 7.0 Hz); 8 lines", with notes when a partner is low-abundance (satellites) or its element has another magnetic isotope that the model treats as non-magnetic (10B beside 11B, 37Cl, 15N/14N...)).
  - `JCouplingSimulationPanel` (`MainWindow.jcoupling_sim_panel`): observe nucleus, field (T, with the 1H and observe frequencies shown), lineshape; auto axis (every line +/-10 FWHM) and auto points (>= 12 per narrowest line); warnings for clipped or under-sampled axes; Export to Open experiments; Copy notebook code (a test `exec`s it and compares).
  - `JCouplingFitPanel` (`MainWindow.jcoupling_fit_panel`): lineshape; "Shift may move +/-" (default 0.05 ppm -- the module docstring's own advice to bound centres, as a default); fit window: *Around the sites* (default: each starting multiplet plus a margin), Range, Integration regions, Whole spectrum; right-click Fix / Set bounds on shift, width and each J. Results table (shift, each J, FWHM Hz, height, area %, chemist notation), R^2/RMSE/reduced chi^2, warnings (J collapsed to 0, shift stopped at its window edge, engine notes), Copy Table / Copy Full Report (the notebook's own report with notation), **Use fitted values as start**, **Open in Simulate** (converts fitted heights to the simulator's area-based intensities so the simulation reproduces the fitted curve -- tested to 1e-4).
- `MainWindow`: `_integration_regions`, `_jcoupling_fit_target` (selected spectrum or displayed slice, as CSA), `_draw_jcoupling_fit` (one continuous range across the windows, shaded per site), `_send_jcoupling_to_simulation`.
- Exports: `spin_multiplet_pattern`, `jcoupling_group_pattern`, `combine_jcouplings`, `multiplet_lineshape`, `jcoupled_spectrum`, `multi_site_jcoupled_spectrum`, `jcoupling_chemist_notation` from `opennmr.notebook`.

### Physics caveats (stated in the GUI, not fixed)

- First order only (no roofing / strong coupling), as the notebook module says.
- A partner's *other* isotopes are treated as spin-0. Right for 13C/12C, 29Si, 195Pt, 117/119Sn; wrong for B (10B, 19.9%, I=3 has its own septet), Cl, Br, Cu, N... The editor flags it; entering 100% abundance models a pure isotope. A proper fix would let a coupling group carry several isotopes with their own J (scaled by gamma).

### Tests

`tests/test_jcoupling.py` (27: patterns from Pascal/spin-1 by hand, 13C satellite weights, convolution, centring regression on even/odd axes, exact lineshape, analytic-vs-grid agreement, multi-site areas, exact triplet and two-site fits, axis-independence regression, fixed J, notation) and `tests/test_gui_jcoupling.py` (20). `test_gui.py`'s section-order lists updated.


## pNMR (CIF): load saved settings, background enumeration, 20x faster runs (2026-09-24, second round)

User: *"make something that will load the saved parameters JSON into the panel, and also run large-volume enumerations in the background"* -- the two follow-ups left open by the round below.

### Measured first

A 4x4x1 supercell of a disordered O3 NaMO2 cell (48 Na sites, 3 shells, 263,424 configurations) took **20.6 s**, of which **13.5 s was `_broadened_spectrum`** -- a Python loop computing an 8192-point Gaussian for every row -- and ~6.6 s enumerating/tabulating, including enumerating all 48 statistically identical Na sites separately. So "run it in the background" alone would have left a 20 s wait; both costs were fixed as well.

### Built

- **Faster, same answers** (`notebook/pnmr_simulator.py`):
  - `_broadened_spectrum` sums rows with identical `Total_shift` (`np.unique` + `bincount`; that case had 364 distinct shifts for 263k rows), then broadens the distinct shifts in vectorised blocks of `_BROADEN_BLOCK` (1024). Exact -- no truncated tails or binning; a test checks it against the one-Gaussian-per-row loop to 1e-12.
  - `enumerate_local_environments` enumerates each distinct environment once (key: per shell, the multiset of neighbour occupancies) and shares the configuration list between sites with that key; `build_shift_table` reuses its rows likewise. Tested against a per-site enumeration done the long way.
  - The same case now runs in **0.9 s** (spectrum identical to 1.2e-14 relative; table contents identical, p to 4e-16). A 6x6x2 supercell (216 sites, 1.19 M configurations) runs in ~4.8 s.
  - Consequences: shift-table **column order is now fixed** (Site, Config, shells in order with species alphabetical, Total_shift, p) instead of whichever order the first configuration produced; and equivalent sites number their Configs in the same (canonical) order. Content is unchanged.
- **Engine hooks**, all optional: `generate_spectrum_dict(progress=, report=, max_configurations=)`. `progress(stage, done, total)` may raise `EnumerationCancelled` to abandon a run (nothing is written); `report` receives the run's warnings instead of print/`warnings.warn` (thread-safe collection); `max_configurations` refuses with `TooManyConfigurations` (carrying the estimate) *before* enumerating. `estimate_configurations()` gives sites / distinct environments / rows / rough bytes cheaply (it counts each shell's compositions, not their product). An unknown nuclide now fails before any work rather than after the enumeration.
- **Parameters files**: `simulation_parameters()`, `save_simulation_parameters(path, **kwargs)`, `load_simulation_parameters(path, cif_filename=None)` -> `generate_spectrum_dict` kwargs, so `nmr.generate_spectrum_dict(**nmr.load_simulation_parameters(p))` reruns a saved simulation. Files now carry `"format": "opennmr.pnmr_simulation_parameters"`, `"version": 1` and the `output_dir` used; files from the first round (no format/version) still load. A CIF that has moved is looked for by name beside the JSON and one folder up (the default output folder is `<cif folder>/pnmr_simulation`), else `FileNotFoundError` naming it.
- **GUI** (`gui/pnmr_panel.py`):
  - *Load settings…* / *Save settings…* in step 1, and a `.json` dropped on the drop zone loads settings. Loading fills every step and Initialises (Enumerate is one click away). What cannot be honoured is listed in one dialog and the log, never dropped silently: sites/species not in the CIF, shifts for species that are no longer contributors, shifts for undefined shells, a non-zero carrier offset or gamma override (the panel always uses 0 / the table value). A species the CIF lacks refuses the load. If the CIF is missing the user is asked to locate it. **The output folder is deliberately not restored**, so rerunning a loaded set-up cannot overwrite the run it came from (the log says so).
  - *Enumerate sites* runs on a worker thread (`PnmrEnumerator`, the `gui/loader.py` pattern: a QObject moved to a lazily-created QThread; synchronous when `OPENNMR_BACKGROUND_LOAD=0`, as under test). A progress bar and stage label; the button becomes **Cancel**, which stops the run at the next site/block (real cancellation, via the progress callback). Every other input is locked while it runs. `MainWindow.closeEvent` calls `pnmr_panel.shutdown()` (cancel + join).
  - A run over `PnmrSimulationPanel.MAX_CONFIGURATIONS` (5 M rows) asks first, quoting the estimate.
  - The load log lists at most 12 site labels (a supercell CIF written by pymatgen labels every atom).

### Tried and rejected

- `multiprocessing` for the enumeration: rejected for the reasons in `gui/loader.py` (spawn on Windows/macOS, PyInstaller, pickling a multi-million-row table back). With the speed-ups above, the GIL-bound thread keeps the window responsive and finishes in seconds for realistic cells.
- Truncating each Gaussian to +/-N sigma or FFT-convolving a binned stick spectrum: faster still, but not exact; the unique-shift aggregation made them unnecessary.

### Still open

- The shift table is still one row per (site, configuration). For very large supercells that table, not the arithmetic, is the limit (~1 GB around 5 M rows). An option to emit one row per *distinct environment* with a site count would shrink it by the number of equivalent sites, but changes the table's format that `pnmr_fit` and saved CSVs rely on -- a decision for the user.
- `warnings.catch_warnings` in the worker (to log pymatgen's CIF-parser notes) is process-wide; a warning raised on the GUI thread during a run would land in that run's log.

### Tests

`tests/test_pnmr_simulator.py` now 51, `tests/test_gui_pnmr.py` 30 (settings round trip -> identical spectrum, JSON drop, moved/missing CIF, what-cannot-be-restored report, limit question both ways, a real background thread: locking, Cancel, window close mid-run).


## Simulate > pNMR (CIF): the notebook's section 5, step by step (2026-09-24)

User: add the CIF "bond pathway" pNMR simulation (`generate_spectrum_dict`) to Simulate, stepwise -- load a CIF (Browse or drag and drop), pick the species to observe from a dropdown, optionally only some of its sites (e.g. C3, C5, C7), "Initialise" once sites of interest and ignored sites are chosen so ignored sites are not offered as contributors, "Add a shell" with radial cutoffs and per-species contributions, broadening (default 1.0 ppm) and field (default 11.7 T), "Enumerate sites", save the table to a chosen `output_dir`, and a "Plot" button with the option to add the result to Open experiments.

### Built

- **`gui/pnmr_panel.py`** (`PnmrSimulationPanel`, `MainWindow.pnmr_panel`), the "pNMR (CIF)" section of the Simulate tile. Five steps plus a log: 1 Structure (Browse / drop zone), 2 Sites (observe, site checklist, ignore species, ignore sites, search radius, *Initialise structure*), 3 Shells (table: name, r min, r max, one column per remaining contributor; *Add shell* suggests limits from the gaps in the distance histogram), 4 Spectrum (nuclide, field, sigma, axis, points, occupancy weighting, output folder, *Enumerate sites*, table preview, *Save table as...*), 5 Plot (+ "Add to Open experiments"). Distance histogram (neighbours per site, stacked by species, occupancy-weighted, shells shaded) on the Simulation plot; the spectrum on the Fit canvas, as the CSA/quadrupolar simulations do.
- **Results are tied to their inputs.** Changing a step-2 choice disables the shell table and Enumerate until Initialise is pressed again; changing anything after Enumerate disables Plot until it is re-run. Plot therefore always shows what the controls say.
- **Engine additions** (`notebook/pnmr_simulator.py`, all exported from `opennmr.notebook`, all optional/backward compatible): site labels in `site_data`; `sites_of_interest=` and `ignore_sites=` on `read_cif_with_occupancies`/`get_neighbors_by_shell`/`shell_distance_histogram`/`generate_spectrum_dict`/`pnmr_fit.predict_environments`; `neighbour_distance_table`, `shell_composition`, `suggest_shell_bins`, `contributing_species`, `site_label_table`, `structure_species`, `candidate_nuclides`, `validate_shell_bins`, `site_weights`, `shift_table_from_structure` (shared by the simulation and `predict_environments`, so the two cannot drift apart). `generate_spectrum_dict` also writes `<nuclide>_simulation_parameters.json` beside the table and records the inputs in `shift_table.attrs["parameters"]`.
- The log shows each step and the exact `generate_spectrum_dict` call; *Copy notebook code* puts it on the clipboard (a test `exec`s it and checks it reproduces the GUI's spectrum).

### Correctness changes to existing behaviour (read these)

1. **Sites are now weighted by occupancy** (`weight_by_occupancy=True`, default). Before, every site of interest counted equally, so a 30%-occupied Na site (P2 Na_f/Na_e) or Li on a TM site (occ 0.05) contributed as much as a full one. Identical results whenever all chosen sites have the same occupancy (e.g. a single-Wyckoff O3 Na site). `weight_by_occupancy=False` restores the old weighting; the GUI has a checkbox.
2. **`real_spectrum` was divided by the number of sites twice** (`build_shift_table` already normalised p over the table; `_broadened_spectrum` divided again). The normalised spectrum was unaffected; the absolute scale now equals the stick probabilities (a test checks peak heights against the binomial weights).
3. **Overlapping shells are refused** (`validate_shell_bins`): `get_neighbors_by_shell` assigns a neighbour to the first matching shell, so an overlap silently under-counted the later shell. Also refused: d_min >= d_max, duplicate/empty names, and shell names that collide with shift-table columns ("p", "Site", "Config", "Total_shift" -- "p" would have overwritten the probability).
4. `generate_spectrum_dict` refuses broadening <= 0, B0 <= 0 and a zero-width xlims, and no longer creates `output_dir` when `save_shift_table=False`.
5. Peaks-outside-xlims warnings are now `PnmrWarning` (a `UserWarning` subclass) so the GUI can show them apart from pymatgen's CIF-parser notes.
6. `notebook/__init__.py`: the uncommitted J-coupling edit had dropped `csa_axis_limits` from the `.simulations` import, so `tests/test_sim_csa_axis.py` failed at collection. Restored. Also, `__all__` had `"SIMPSONread_fid" "SIMPSONplot_fid"` (missing comma -- one concatenated, non-existent name). Fixed.

### Known semantics, documented rather than changed

- `ignore_species` drops a neighbour **site** if *any* occupant is ignored, so ignoring Br- on a Cl/Br-shared site also removes the Cl-. The panel says so after Initialise ("Also left out, ...").
- The model treats every neighbour position's occupancy as independent (random solid solution), including two images of the same cell site.
- pymatgen merges a position shared by several CIF rows into one site with one of those rows' labels (e.g. `X1`/`X1b` -> `X1b`).

### Tests

`tests/test_pnmr_simulator.py` (32) and `tests/test_gui_pnmr.py` (18), both `importorskip("pymatgen")`. Analytic cases: a rock-salt Na(Cl0.5Br0.5) cell (binomial(6, 1/2) shifts, 6/12 neighbour counts, suggested shells), and a P1 cell with Na1 (occ 1) and Na2 (occ 0.5) for site choice and weighting. pymatgen is **not** a declared dependency (it is imported lazily; the panel explains how to install it) -- added as the `pnmr` extra and to `test`.

### Not built (possible next steps)

- Load settings back from a saved `*_simulation_parameters.json`.
- Running Enumerate off the GUI thread (a large supercell with many disordered neighbours enumerates slowly; it currently runs with a wait cursor).


## Dark-mode fixes, a theme toggle, tiles on top, quadrupolar nucleus (2026-09-23)

User, on the soft-edge sheet from the round below: *"A lot of the small buttons like the up/down arrows are really messed up in the dark mode, and many buttons have no distinction from the background colour."* Plus: *"add a toggle in settings to switch between light and dark modes (default is still system settings)"*, *"the big buttons should be a persistent row along the top of the app"*, and *"ensure that the quadrupolar simulation nucleus is the same kind of box as for PFG (dropdown but editable) and reads the nuclear spin directly from the table to avoid mismatches"*.

### Three measurements, three causes

Everything below was diagnosed by measuring, because all three symptoms had plausible wrong explanations.

* **"No distinction from the background."** `palette(button)` is **byte-identical to `palette(window)`** on this platform -- #efefef both, contrast **1.00:1** -- so painting a button `background: palette(button)` made it invisible. `style.py` now *builds* the palette instead of reading ambiguous roles from the platform's, with `Button` deliberately offset from `Window` and a distinct mid-grey **border** role (the thing that actually makes a button read as one: light **1.47:1** against the window, dark **2.20:1**). A test pins those ratios.
* **"Up/down arrows really messed up."** A stylesheet rule on a widget class drops it out of the native renderer for *every* property, so a styled `QSpinBox` paints no arrows unless every sub-control is respecified with its own `image:`. `QSpinBox`, `QDoubleSpinBox`, `QComboBox`, `QSlider`, `QScrollBar`, `QCheckBox`, `QRadioButton` and `QHeaderView` are now in a named `_NEVER_STYLED` list and absent from the sheet -- listed rather than merely omitted so a later edit has to delete one first. They take their softening from the palette.
* **A full-suite failure the same sheet caused.** `test_ui_font_size_scales_the_interface_and_keeps_titles_ahead` broke: `output_colormap_combo` stayed at 9pt while the app font went to 15pt. Bisected to **any** application stylesheet -- one naming only `QGroupBox` does it too -- marking existing widgets' fonts as explicitly set. Fix is `style.refresh_fonts()`, re-applying the *same* sheet after `setFont`, called from `_apply_ui_font_size`. **Clearing the sheet first does not work** (measured: widgets stay at the stale size); only the re-set re-resolves them.

### Built

* **Appearance toggle** in Settings ▸ Interface: Follow system / Light / Dark, saved to the UI settings JSON. "Follow system" resolves to the matching palette rather than leaving the platform's alone, so the guaranteed button contrast holds in every mode. `_apply_ui_theme` also asks each canvas to restyle, tolerating a canvas that has no `set_theme`.
* **Launcher tiles as a persistent full-width row** above both columns. New `WrappingTabWidget.takeTabBar()` reparents the strip out; it still drives the stack because the wiring is signal-based, not positional. The splitter is no longer the central widget, so it is exposed as `window.main_splitter`.
* **Quadrupolar nucleus** is now an editable `QComboBox` matching the PFG simulator's, offering only **I ≥ 1** nuclides (a spin-1/2 has no quadrupole moment, so listing one would offer an impossible simulation) and filling **Spin I from the nuclide table** on change. New `core.registry.find_spin()` and `quadrupolar_nuclides()`; `find_gamma()` gained a `spin` key. The handler is silent on unrecognised text because it fires per keystroke -- "2" on the way to "23Na" must not warn or reset.

### Round 2: the theme was only half applied

Tried the above in a dark-mode OS and reported, in light mode: *"background behind the mpl controls is still dark, the file dropdown arrows are white, as are the arrows in the spinboxes, background of the phase up/down arrow buttons is still dark, many fonts like in the table and eg the export curve fit (CSV) button are light grey"*, then *"And the phase pivot bar too"*.

**Every one of those was the same cause, and it was the fix above biting back.** The widgets deliberately left out of the stylesheet (`_NEVER_STYLED`) are drawn by the *platform* style, which on macOS follows the **operating system's** appearance and ignores `QPalette` for its sub-controls. Confirmed: `defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle` -> `Dark`. So with the OS dark and openNMR set to light, the combo/spin arrows, the `pivot_slider` (a plain `QSlider`), the matplotlib `NavigationToolbar2QT` background and the table text all kept rendering in the system appearance. Not styling them fixed the arrows and cost them the theme.

`apply_theme` now installs the **Fusion** style, which resolves those sub-controls from the palette, so one palette decides the whole window; plus `styleHints().setColorScheme()` (Qt 6.11 here) for chrome Fusion does not draw. **Cost, stated plainly: the app no longer looks natively macOS.** That is the price of a toggle that works at all -- the native style cannot be repainted into an appearance the OS is not in.

A latent bug fell out of the same change: `apply_theme` *sets* the colour scheme, so "follow system" would have read its own last choice back and latched onto it. `remember_system_theme()` samples the platform once at startup, before anything overrides it, and `system_prefers_dark` reads that rather than `styleHints()`.

### Round 3: the one widget no style can reach

*"The phasing buttons are still dark in light mode, maybe make them blue like the headings?"* -- `DragHandle.paintEvent` painted with **literal** colours (fill `QColor(80, 80, 80)`, glyph `QColor(220, 220, 220)`). No palette, style or stylesheet can reach a literal, so it was dark in both themes and always had been. Now drawn from `palette(Highlight)` with `HighlightedText` for the glyph -- the accent blue the user asked for -- and it gained hover/pressed states it never had. A test greps `paintEvent` for `QColor(` so a literal cannot creep back. It was the **only** custom-painted widget in `gui/`; checked, not assumed.

### Round 4: two follow-ups on the quadrupolar box

* *"shouldn't let spin be editable also, just set by nucleus"* -- `sim_quad_spin_spin` is now `setReadOnly(True)` with `NoButtons` and no focus. Read-only rather than disabled, so the value stays at full contrast and legible.
* **A regression the full suite caught**, worth recording because the mistake is easy to repeat: converting the nucleus `QLineEdit` to a `QComboBox` silently broke the "seeded, never forced" logic, which tests `if not <field text>`. A combo with items is **never** empty -- it starts on item 0 -- so seeding stopped happening and the box always read `2H`. Fixed with `setCurrentIndex(-1)`, which on an editable combo gives a genuinely empty line edit and restores the original semantics. Tightened at the same time: a **spin-1/2 spectrum no longer seeds it at all**, because filling it with 31P would pair a nuclide this simulation cannot run with a Spin I describing a different one -- the exact mismatch reading I from the table exists to prevent.

### Open

* The dark palette is hand-picked, not derived from the system accent colour; a user with a non-blue accent still gets openNMR's blue highlight.

### Settled, not open

Both raised as trade-offs and both decided by the user, recorded here so they are not re-litigated as oversights:

* **Plots stay light in every theme.** A figure here is the same object that gets exported, and an exported figure belongs on white -- so a dark interface wraps light plots and what you see is what you export. *"Figure should still always be light I should think."* `_apply_ui_theme` therefore touches only the interface palette; the speculative `canvas.set_theme` hook an earlier draft called was removed rather than left implying a future dark canvas. Revisiting this means separating on-screen colours from export colours first: one setting cannot serve both.
* **Fusion is forced unconditionally**, so the app looks the same on every OS rather than native on each. *"Fusion is good, a constant aesthetic is good across OSs."* No native-style escape hatch.
* `_apply_ui_theme` calls `canvas.set_theme` if it exists -- **no canvas implements one yet**, so matplotlib figures stay light-on-white inside a dark interface. That is the obvious next piece and is deliberately not guessed at here.
* The combo offers the first 24 quadrupolar nuclides by mass number; the table has 90. Anything else can still be typed, but there is no search.
* Still unverified on Windows/Linux, as below.


## Spinsolve preview, softer edges, and Compare's scroll-to-scale (2026-09-23)

User, after pulling `euan-merge`: *"the new spinsolve data loads and can be processed but there is no processing preview available. Also right now all the buttons are very harsh and squared, can the edges be softened a bit? For compare, the x-axis scroll to zoom is a bit of an issue when there are lots of spectra stacked and you want to scale the y intensity."*

Also fixed on the way in: two defects that arrived with the branch. `tests/test_wrapping_tabs.py` carried a **stray `=======` from an unresolved merge conflict** in `01d854f` -- a syntax error that blocked collection of the entire suite, and had been on `euan-merge` for eight commits. Both sides' tests were distinct, so both were kept. `tests/test_gui.py` asserted the old literal status-bar string, which `6cdbfdf` correctly generalised when it added per-value source tags. **CI never caught either: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` only triggers on `main`.** Adding `euan-merge` to that trigger list is the obvious follow-up and is *not* done.

### 1. Spinsolve had no processing preview

Two gates, both closed. `_raw_fid_reprocessing_available` is a hard-coded vendor allowlist that did not include `"spinsolve"`, and `read_spectrum` deliberately withheld `fid`/`fid_raw`/`fid_dt` -- on the stated reasoning that the generic reprocessing path "has no way to apply this format's conjugate -- it would put the peak at the mirrored shift."

**Measured, that reasoning was half wrong.** `processing.ft.fft_spectrum` builds a *descending* frequency axis (`-fftshift(fftfreq)`), which is the same mirroring the reader's `fft(conj(fid))` achieved: pushed through the generic path the peak lands at **0.2207 ppm**, exactly where the reader puts it. Not mirrored at all. What the two *did* differ by was subtler and worse for a live preview: the generic path returned the **complex conjugate, one bin over** (the one bin being the even-length `fftshift` reversal the adapter's `[::-1]` introduced). Real parts agreed; imaginary parts were negated -- so a phase drag would have rotated the preview opposite to the Spectrum tab.

Fixed at the root rather than papered over: `SpinsolvePFG.spectra()` now goes through `ft.apodize`/`ft.zero_fill`/`ft.fft_spectrum` instead of a hand-rolled `fftshift(fft(conj(fid)))`, and `ppm_axis()` descends like every other vendor's, so the adapter's reversal is gone. Reader and preview now agree to **1e-9** once the instrument's recorded phase (-0.50 deg here) is removed -- and every vendor works that way, the loaded spectrum carrying the recorded phase while the preview starts unphased. Still reproduces `fit.csv`: D 1.33526e-10 vs 1.338e-10 (0.20%), I0 82.169 vs 82.116 (0.065%).

### 2. Buttons were hard-edged

**Nothing in `src/opennmr/gui/` set a `border-radius` anywhere.** New `gui/style.py`: `soft_edges_qss(radius=6)` plus `apply_soft_edges(app)`, called from `app.main()` and from `MainWindow.__init__` (idempotent via a marker comment) so an embedded window and the test suite look like the packaged app.

Deliberately minimal, and the reason is a real constraint rather than taste: **on macOS, styling any property of a widget class drops that class out of the native renderer for every property**, so an over-specified sheet turns a native app flat. The sheet therefore sets corner radius, border and padding only, and takes every colour from `palette()` roles -- no literal colour appears in it, which a test asserts -- so system light/dark and the user's accent colour still come through. `RADIUS = 6` / `CONTAINER_RADIUS = 8` are the only knobs; 0 restores the old squares.

### 3. Compare's scroll-to-scale, measured

`_hovering_x_axis` tested `event.y < bbox.y0` -- **unbounded below**. In a stacked Compare (one axes per row, `hspace=0.0`) the region under one row *is* the next row down, so every inter-row gap claimed the x-zoom. Swept vertically down a 12-row stack, 60 sample points:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| scaled intensity | 42% (and interleaved `xxBxBBxBBxBxxB…`) | **83%** |
| zoomed x | 52% | 17% (the real tick strip) |
| did nothing | 5% | **0%** |

Two changes. `_x_strip_depth(ax)` bounds the strip to the decorations that are actually there, via `get_tightbbox()`: a stacked row that draws no tick labels (every row but the bottom, sharing one x axis) gets **zero** depth and so claims nothing. A panel with nothing below it keeps the old unbounded behaviour, which is every single-panel view -- aiming below the axis label still works there, pinned by its own test. Second, the `_compare_axes` intensity branch moved **above** the `event.ydata is None` guard, and the `ax is None` early return now lets a Compare through: that branch reads no cursor y and no `ax`, rescaling each row from its own ylim, so the gaps can drive it. A stacked Compare is the one view with no meaningful "nowhere".

### Open

* The `euan-merge` CI trigger (above).
* `RADIUS` is not user-configurable from the GUI; it is a constant in `gui/style.py`. A Settings control is the obvious next step if 6px is not the right number.
* The soft-edge sheet has not been eyeballed on Windows or Linux, only reasoned about -- the palette-role approach is what should make it portable, but nobody has looked.


## Bruker PFG gradients without a diff.xml (2026-09-23)

User: *"plan out a better way to include bruker gradient info if the diff module is not used to create the experiment (ie no diff.xml file). They should still use difflist which is the gradient strengths in G/cm. Maybe this can also read the associated pp and pull out the values for delta ... and DELTA ... Prepare this method for easy integration with either the current GUI or the soon-to-be-merged one"*

### Built

`src/opennmr/io/bruker_pfg.py` and `tests/test_bruker_pfg.py` (15 tests). **Nothing existing was edited** -- same containment as the Spinsolve round, for the same merge reason. Entry point `read_pfg_params(path)` -> `BrukerPFG`, which resolves the gradient axis *whether or not* there is a `diff.xml` and tags every value with where it came from (`.sources`) plus anything the caller should know before trusting it (`.warnings`).

### The trap that had to be closed first

**`difflist` does not always hold gradients.** The user's premise -- "difflist ... is the gradient strengths in G/cm" -- is right for the `dosy`-AU case and *wrong* for the diff-module case, which was worth checking before building on it:

| set up via | `difflist` holds | range |
|---|---|---|
| `dosy` AU (`ledbpgp2s`, no `diff.xml`) | gradient amplitude, **G/cm** | 1 .. 51 |
| TopSpin diff module (`diffSte`, `diffDste`) | **b-values, s/m^2** | 9.6e7 .. 3.8e10 |

Verified: on `bruker_PFG/150` and `Diff50.../11`, `difflist` equals `diff.xml`'s own `B` digit for digit. Reading those as G/cm would give gradients of 1e8 G/cm and a b-axis out by twenty orders of magnitude -- and would still fit. `read_difflist` decides from the diff-module's own files (`diff.xml`/`diffConf.xml`/`diffHistory.txt`) with a magnitude guard behind it, and **returns which it is** rather than letting the caller assume.

### delta and DELTA from the pulse programme

Bruker's stock sequences document their own parameters in a trailing comment block, so nothing is keyed on a parameter *number*:

```
;p30: gradient pulse (little DELTA * 0.5)
;d20: diffusion time (big DELTA)
;d16: delay for gradient recovery
```

`describe_diffusion_pulseprogram` matches Bruker's own wording ("little DELTA", "big DELTA"/"diffusion time", "gradient recovery"). **The `* 0.5` is why the wording is parsed rather than the name**: on a bipolar sequence p30 is half of delta, and taking it as delta understates b by 4x. Bipolar-ness is read **structurally** from the body (`p30:gp6*-1*diff` -- the same pulse replayed negated on one channel), not from the sequence name, and that also yields the gradient channel (6) for the `gpnam`/`GPZ` lookups. A programme documenting none of this comes back `resolved = False` rather than guessing -- which is exactly what the diff-module sequences do, and they have a `diff.xml` instead.

### The shape factor is already in difflist -- do not apply it twice

The `dosy` AU writes `difflist = gradient_calib x SHAPE_INTEGFAC x GPZ/100 x Difframp`. On the reference dataset that identity holds to **1e-5**: `53.5 G/cm x 0.97737556561086 x 1.00 x Difframp == difflist`. So `difflist` is the *effective*, shape-corrected amplitude and the b-value must be taken with `shape="rect"`. Applying `smsq10` on top would double-count and understate D by 0.9^2 = 19%. `read_pfg_params` rebuilds that product from the four files and **warns** if it ever fails to reproduce `difflist`; passing `shape=` explicitly also warns. Note `gpnam6` here is `Difftrap`, not the `SMSQ10.100` the pulse programme's comment suggests -- another reason not to take the shape from the sequence's documentation.

### Verified

`test_data/NMR400_KT_DPC_ALSK_AL_70B_3/10` (`ledbpgp2s`, 1H, 32 steps, 298.0 K): delta = 2 x p30 = **4.42 ms**, DELTA = d20 = **60 ms**, tau = d16 = **0.2 ms**, gradients **1.046 .. 51.244 G/cm**, b **8.94e6 .. 2.15e10 s/m^2**. Fitting the solute's three resolved peaks (0.09, 0.24, 0.34 ppm) gives **D = 1.78e-10 m^2/s** with the three agreeing to **<1%** and rmse 1.4% of I0. There is no `diff.xml` to check against, so the b-axis is pinned by that internal consistency plus the `difflist` reconstruction above.

### Ready for the GUI, not wired to it

Three seams exist already and none were touched:

1. `BrukerPFG.as_pfg_params()` returns the same flat seconds dict as `processing.diffusion.pfg_params_from_metadata`, which is what `_on_read_pfg_params_clicked` consumes -- so the Bruker branch is a call swap, not new GUI code. (That handler's current message even tells the user to "use a diff.xml instead"; this removes the need.)
2. The values-source "Auto" path (`main_window.py` ~13930) does `read_diff_xml(...)["B"]` inside a `try: except FileNotFoundError`. `read_pfg_params(path).b` covers both branches in one call.
3. `.sources` / `.warnings` are strings meant to be shown, so the GUI can say *where* delta came from rather than presenting a bare number.

### Open

* Only **one** `dosy`-AU dataset exists in `test_data/`. The monopolar branch (`;p30: gradient pulse (little DELTA)`, `ledgp2s`/`stegp1s`) is implemented and unit-tested on synthetic text, but never against a real file.
* **tau is taken as `d16` alone.** Strictly the bipolar inter-lobe delay also contains the 180 pulse (p2 = 24 us here), which would make tau 224 us rather than 200. Measured effect on b: **0.02%**. Recorded rather than modelled; resolving `p2=p1*2` out of the programme body is a parser rabbit hole for a number well under the fit's own uncertainty.
* **The solvent's D looks low.** CHCl3 at 7.29 ppm fits 1.61e-9 m^2/s against a neat-liquid literature ~2.3e-9 at 25 C. The solute dominates the spectrum ~40:1, so genuine obstruction/viscosity in a concentrated solution is the likely explanation and the solute's own D is internally consistent -- but a neat-solvent or water-standard dataset acquired the same way is what would actually settle whether `gradient_calib`'s 5.35 G/mm is still true for this probe. `calibrate_max_gradient` already exists for exactly that.
* `Oneshot` sequences are not special-cased: they would resolve as `bipolar`, which is what `processing.diffusion` models for them anyway (the unbalancing factor is deliberately not modelled there).


## Spinsolve PGSTE reader, standalone (2026-09-23)

User: *"I have added some spinsolve PFG data to the test_data folder, I want you to figure out how to parse the raw data and any associated diffusion information in the folder. I don't need to have this added to the GUI yet, since we will soon merge Euan's updated version with this one, so just work on this as an independent function for now."*

### Built

`src/opennmr/io/spinsolve.py` and `tests/test_spinsolve.py` (11 tests). **Deliberately not registered** with `io.base` and not imported by `io/__init__.py`, so it cannot conflict with Euan's merge -- wiring it in later is one `base.register()` call plus an `NMRSpectrum` adapter. Entry point `read_spinsolve_pfg(folder)` -> `SpinsolvePFG`, with `find_spinsolve_experiments(root)` to walk a Spinsolve date tree and `selftest(folder)` to re-run the checks below on a new dataset.

### What the format turned out to be

A PGSTE folder holds the same matrix **four times** and the diffusion axis **twice**:

* `data.2d` -- **the raw FID**, and the one to read. Prospa V1.1 binary: 32-byte header, then five `int32` (`dataType`, nx, ny, nz, nq), then the data. The magic reads `SORPATAD1.1V` on disk because it is three 4-char tags (`PROS`, `DATA`, `V1.1`) each stored **byte-reversed**. `dataType` 501 = interleaved complex float32; `data.1d` is 504 = a float32 x-axis column *then* interleaved complex float32, and holds whichever single row the UI had selected (`display.par`'s `StackIndex`).
* `data.2d.bin` -- the same numbers as **big-endian int64 in units of 1e-4**, blocked (every real, then every imaginary) rather than interleaved. Agrees with `data.2d` to exactly half a quantum, which is what pins the scale factor as exactly 1e4 rather than approximately.
* `data_enhanced.2d` -- Spinsolve's **already-apodized** copy (one window applied identically to every row, plus a linear phase ramp). Same shape as the raw FID, so it is easy to read by mistake; `source=` selects it explicitly.
* `delayTimes.txt` -- **a misnomer inherited from the T1/T2 protocols.** For PGSTE it holds the **b-values** in s/m^2, not delays. Written in the acquiring PC's locale, so here `2,600749E+07` -- comma decimal separator.
* `data.2d.txt` -- DOSY Toolbox ASCII header. The only place the **gradient amplitude array (T/m)**, gamma, and the true delta/DELTA appear.

### The traps

* **`acqu.par`'s `littleDelta` is not delta.** It is 3 ms, the plateau; the sequence plays 3.1 ms, `littleDelta + gradRamp`. Using 3 ms puts D out by 7%. `data.2d.txt`'s "Diffusion Encoding Time" is the value to trust; the reader falls back to `littleDelta + gradRamp` only when that file is missing.
* **The FT needs a conjugate.** `fftshift(fft(fid))` on an ascending-ppm axis puts this sample's single peak at **9.25 ppm**; `fftshift(fft(conj(fid)))` puts it at **0.22 ppm**, inside the integral region `display.par` records and where `data.jpg` shows it. Both look like spectra, so this is pinned by a test rather than left to inspection.
* **Intensities need the `1/n` FFT scaling** (n = the zero-filled length) to be comparable with `fit.csv`'s A.
* `acqu.par` keys can start with a digit (`90PulseLength`), values carry **unescaped inner quotes** (`graphTitle`), and `display.par` contains a stray key-less `= 0` line. All three are handled rather than raising.

### Verified against the instrument's own answers

Reading `data.2d`, applying the 1 Hz exponential from `display.par`, zero-filling 4x (`acqu.par`'s `zeroFill`), FTing and integrating `display.par`'s own region reproduces `fit.csv`:

| | openNMR | Spinsolve | |
|---|---|---|---|
| D | 1.33864e-10 m^2/s | 1.338e-10 | **0.05%** |
| I0 | 82.210 | 82.116 | **0.11%** |

and b recomputed from the gradient array matches `delayTimes.txt` to **1.2e-5** relative.

### Reused, not rewritten

The b-value and the fit both delegate to `processing/diffusion.py` (`b_value`, `build_diffusion_model`) and `processing/relaxation.py` (`fit_relaxation`) -- the same engine the Bruker and X-Pulse PFG paths use -- so Spinsolve gets multi-component, stretched and log-space-D fitting and typed uncertainties without any of it being written twice. Only the b-axis and the integrals are this module's own work. `gamma` is stored in **Hz/T** to match that engine; `data.2d.txt` states it in rad s^-1 T^-1 and is converted on read.

### Open

* Only **one** Spinsolve dataset exists in `test_data/` (1H, PGSTE CDEC, 64 steps). The `dataType` codes 500/502/503 and the non-1H gamma path are implemented but unexercised.
* The **per-step phase sign** (`exp(+i*ph0)` vs `exp(-i*ph0)`) cannot be settled from this dataset: every `phaseShifts.txt` entry is within 0.3 degrees of zero, so both conventions fit equally well. A visibly mis-phased dataset would settle it.
* The exact window `data_enhanced.2d` carries was not reverse-engineered -- it rises then falls, so it is some Lorentz-to-Gauss-like enhancement, but `display.par` only records a 1 Hz exponential. Since the raw FID is right there, it was not worth chasing.
* Not wired into the GUI, `io.base`, or `NMRSpectrum`, on purpose (see above).

## CSA lineshape fitting in the GUI, and Euan's simple requests (2026-09-19)

**Supersedes the plan written earlier the same day**, which was drafted without knowing PR #1 existed. That plan proposed building multi-model fitting support and per-parameter bounds from scratch; Euan has already written both, so stages 1-3 of it are moot. What follows replaces it.

### What arrived, and what it changes

PR #1's `src/opennmr/notebook/` is now on main (commit "Take Euan's notebook package from PR #1, without its reverts" -- the PR itself must **not** be merged, see that commit message). For CSA specifically:

* `csa_fitting.fit_csa_spectrum` is a complete **multi-site** fitter: labels, per-site bounds, per-site fixed matrices, a robust fixed baseline, bound-hit detection, a report and a plotting routine. Parameter layout is five per site -- `d_iso, span_or_Delta, skew_or_eta, fwhm, A` -- followed by `b0, b1`.
* `simulations` gains **ZCW powder averaging**. This is what makes the whole thing practical: a ZCW grid reaches a given accuracy from far fewer orientations than a rectangular theta/phi one, and the powder loop is what dominates the cost of every fit iteration.

### The architecture decision: a dedicated path, not a refactor

The earlier plan's stage 2 was to teach `processing/fitting.py` about simulated models so a CSA line could sit in the peak table beside Gaussians. **Rejected.** The peak table is pseudo-Voigt-shaped -- shift, FWHM, eta -- and a CSA site is delta_iso, span/Delta, skew/eta, FWHM plus a convention; forcing them into one table distorts both, and `fit_csa_spectrum` already *is* the fitter, with its own parameter layout and bounds machinery.

Instead CSA gets its own path, exactly the shape DOSY, SCORE and eNMR already have in this GUI: a dialog, an Analysis action, its own results label, and a view on the shared Fit canvas. That is the house pattern, and it reuses Euan's code whole rather than reimplementing it -- the standing rule.

### Work items

1. ~~**A bridge from `NMRSpectrum` to the notebook's results dict.**~~ **Built.** `notebook/bridge.py`, `results_from_spectrum(spectrum, row=None)`. Every notebook entry point -- `fit_csa_spectrum`, and later pNMR, BMS and SIMPSON -- takes the ten-key dict `NMR1dimport` returns (`x_ppm`, `real_spectrum`, `normalised_real_spectrum`, `SFO1`, `nuclide`, ...), and nothing in `src/` outside `notebook/` produces one. This is the seam between the live application and the notebook API, so it belongs in its own module rather than buried in a GUI handler: `notebook/bridge.py`, `results_from_spectrum(spectrum)`.

2. ~~**Read the MAS rate.**~~ **Built, and it needed no new plumbing at all** -- Bruker writes `MASR` into `acqus` and the reader already carries that to `metadata.raw`, so the control just needed somewhere to read it. Seeded on selection, never forced: a rate recorded at setup and not used is common. Original note follows. The finite-MAS model needs it and **nothing outside `notebook/` reads `MASR`** -- `acquisition_constants` does not expose it, and `io/bruker.py` never parses it. Read it per vendor into metadata, and default the dialog's control from it.

3. ~~**The CSA fit dialog.**~~ **Built as a sub-tab, not a dialog** -- Analysis > CSA, beside Curve Fitting/eNMR/VOCS/Imaging, which is where the other analyses live. Sites table, convention, static/finite-MAS, powder scheme and *two* orientation counts. A sites table (label, delta_iso, span/Delta, skew/eta, FWHM, fixed), a Haeberlen <-> Herzfeld-Berger toggle, static vs finite-MAS with the rate, and the powder controls. Powder resolution matters enough to be visible rather than hidden: coarse while fitting, refined for the final render, which is what `csa_fitting`'s own docstring advises.

4. ~~**Handler, render, report.**~~ **Built.** The curve draws through the existing `show_slice_fit` rather than a CSA-specific twin of it -- it already draws "measured plus fitted, optionally with per-component shading", and a CSA fit is exactly that with one component per site. The report is Euan's own `print_csa_fit_report`, captured from stdout rather than reimplemented. Run the fit, keep the result beside the other analysis results, draw it on the Fit canvas through the existing "Showing:" switcher, and print `print_csa_fit_report` into a `csa_results_label` of its own -- per-sub-tab labels being the convention since the reports moved out of `analysis_results_label`.

5. **Validate against DMFit, not a fixture.** `test_data/2p5mm_.../2012/pdata/1/` holds real DMFit fits of the 23Na/113Cd data, including `FIT_6lines_1CSA_2Quad1st_3GaussLor_Best_Yet_20260506`. The `dmfit` reader exists in `leonmr.py:373` and is on the survey backlog. **This is the X-Pulse F1 lesson applied before the fact**: a self-built fixture agreed with a wrong reader for four rounds there, and an external reference settled it in one pass. A powder lineshape that looks plausible and is wrong is the same trap.

### Found while building it

* **A clipped powder pattern fits back with a badly shrunken span, and nothing else says so.** Measured directly: the same tensor fitted over a window that cuts its high-frequency shoulder returns Δ = 126 ppm against a true 200, because the residual *inside* the window stays small. The fitted span is the number people take away from a CSA fit, so the CSA tab now warns when the fitted lineshape still has more than 5% of its height at the edge of the fitted range. There is a test for it.
* **Euan's fitter is exact.** `csa_model_full` reproduces `make_static_csa_spectrum` to 0.0 difference, and a fit started away from the answer recovers a known tensor exactly (δiso 100.0, Δ 200.0, η 0.30 from a start of 85/170/0.45). An earlier apparent failure was the clipping above, in the test's own window -- not the code.
* **FWHM absorbs the powder grid's graininess.** Fitting on a coarse grid inflates the fitted linewidth (10.7 ppm against a true 5.0 at 800 orientations) while leaving the tensor parameters exact. That is the trade the two orientation counts exist to manage, and it is why the tests assert the tensor tightly and the linewidth not at all.

### Deferred: quadrupolar fitting

`simulations` models static quadrupolar lineshapes three ways plus a MAS FID, but there is still **no quadrupolar fitting module** -- `csa_fitting.py` has no counterpart, and Euan's PR did not add one. Most of the DMFit reference fits are quadrupolar, so this is the larger prize; it should follow CSA, which proves the path on the simpler interaction.

### Euan's written requests: the two simple ones

From `notes_from_Euan.txt`. The rest of that list is mostly addressed already; these two are not, and both are small.

* **Signal-to-noise threshold for peak picking.** Currently the only sensitivity control is Min. prominence (`auto_pick_prominence_spin`). His point is that prominence alone fails exactly where it matters: *"prominence can become v small when you have strong and weak peaks (e.g., decomposition products in the baseline of electrolytic solutions)"* -- a percentage-of-maximum threshold cannot express "above the noise" when one peak dwarfs the rest. Plan: an optional **Min. S/N** spin beside prominence, with the noise estimated the way the baseline fitter already estimates it (`estimate_baseline_robust`'s sigma-clipped residual), so the two agree about what "noise" means. Both filters apply, so it narrows rather than replaces.
* **Mass in mg by default.** Mass is stored in **grams** (`NMRMetadata.mass`, documented as g) and `_refresh_selection_display` already renders it as mg (`meta.mass * 1000.0`), so only the *input* is left in grams. Plan: the mass field takes mg and divides by 1000 on the way in, so the unit reads the same in both directions. Small, but it is a units bug waiting to happen -- someone types 50 meaning 50 mg and gets 50 g, and mass-normalised comparison then scales that spectrum by a factor of 1000.

## The indirect dimension: axis direction, and a window it never had (2026-09-18, eighteenth round)

User: *"The indirect dimension appears to be inverted somehow and I don't think the windowing is being applied to the indirect dimension, and certainly I don't see the windowing in the processing view."* Three things, all true, none of them caused by the TPPI round below.

### The F1 axis direction: changed, wrong, changed back

This one took two goes, and the second one was the revert.

`plot_2d_contour` called `ax.invert_yaxis()` for every genuine 2D. On the first report ("the indirect dimension appears to be inverted somehow") that looked like the cause, and it was removed -- on the reading that both frequency axes should increase toward the top-left. **That reading was wrong**, and the user restated the convention directly: *"the vertical axis the wrong way round (low to high, bottom to top) compared to the horizontal axis (NMR convention low to high, right to left)"*.

The rule is that **values increase in the negative screen direction on both axes**. F2 increases right-to-left (`invert_xaxis`, universal); F1 increases top-to-bottom for exactly the same reason. High ppm at the left *and* at the bottom, and a homonuclear spectrum's nQ = 1 line running bottom-left to top-right. `invert_yaxis()` is back, in `plot_2d_contour` and `overlay_plot` alike.

**Nothing in the code distinguishes the two orientations**, which is the real lesson here: the data lands at identical *coordinates* either way, the nQ line is drawn in data space so it passes through the self-correlations either way, and every existing test passed under both. Only an explicit assertion holds the convention, so there is now one, plus a second test checking a self-correlation lands on the drawn nQ = 1 line in *display* coordinates.

What the original "inverted" report was actually about is the item below: with no F1 window, truncation ringing dragged the apparent F1 maximum off the diagonal (4.61 against F2's 4.74) and smeared a streak through the whole indirect dimension. Windowing put it back at 4.74 exactly.

### F1 is States-TPPI quadrature, settled against MestReNova

Three rounds were spent inferring F1's encoding from two datasets that cannot distinguish the possibilities, in front of a user who kept saying it was still wrong. It ended when they exported the same NOESY from **MestReNova** at four stages -- unprocessed FID, processed FID, after the first FT, and finished -- which answered it in one pass.

**The decisive fact was a row count.** `Processed_FID_1st_FT.csv` holds **128 non-zero rows out of 256**: MNova halves the acquired FIDs before zero-filling. So F1's quadrature is **States** -- a cos-modulated FID and a sin-modulated one at each t1 -- which with F2's own quadrature makes **four pages per t1 increment**. The `##PAGE= T1=` labels (3, 253, 503, ...) increment per page-pair, which is exactly why this looked like one t1 point per pair and why it was ruled out twice; they are a per-page counter, and the true t1 advances once per cos/sin pair.

That also dissolves the argument the previous rounds were stuck in. Genuine quadrature gives a single peak **and** the full sweep width -- the two were never a trade. MNova's finished F1: 256 points, 1298.501 -> -693.686 Hz (the full 2000 Hz, the same window as F2), single peak at 4.74 ppm with the next feature at 0.06 of it.

Measured against MNova's own F1 profile:

| decode | correlation |
|---|---|
| States-TPPI (`fn_mode` 5), no sign flip, no reversal | **+0.85** |
| plain States (`fn_mode` 4) | -0.04, every peak thrown to the axis edges |
| amplitude-modulated, no decode (what had been shipping) | +0.0006, mirrored |

After it: F1 projection peak **4.74 ppm against MNova's 4.74**, and the solvent self-correlation sits **0.02 ppm off the diagonal**.

**What had gone wrong is that the two halves of the fix were never held at once.** The original reader did the States decode but treated the raw pages as the cos/sin pair, so F2 mirrored. Fixing that -- combining R + iI into one complex FID, which is right and stays -- and *removing* the decode fixed F2 and broke F1. Both steps are needed.

Everything built on the TPPI reading is gone: `tppi_f1_spectrum`, `tppi_f1_mask`, `tppi_f1_length`, `tppi_f1_interferogram_length`, `XPULSE_TPPI_RAMP_SIGN`, `XPULSE_TPPI_CROP`, and the GUI branches keyed on `f1_transform`. The reader now records `f1_quadrature_sign_flip: False` instead, because the GUI's own rebuild applies Bruker's `data[1::2] *= -1` normalisation for `fn_mode` 4/5 and X-Pulse must not -- a divergence that predates this round and would have made the live rebuild disagree with the load.

**The lesson worth keeping: a synthetic fixture cannot settle a format question.** This fixture was rebuilt three times, and each time it agreed with whatever the reader was doing, because the same wrong assumption went into both. It now carries States-TPPI pairs with `(cos, -sin)` sense, checked against the constraint that a homonuclear fixture's own diagonal peak must land at the same label in both dimensions. The regression that actually holds this is `test_the_noesy_matches_mestrenovas_own_processing`, which compares against the export rather than against a model.

**Still open:** MNova's F1 peak is narrower than this reader's. MNova also applies backward LP and F1 linear prediction (`LPBIN= 512`) and this does not, and F1 is unphased here. Separate work.

### F1 had no window at all

Not in either X-Pulse reader, and in the GUI's live rebuild only as Bruker's own recorded `proc2s` WDW, with nothing the user could choose for any vendor. An interferogram cut off at its last increment rings as sinc wiggles down F1, and **F1 is where truncation hurts most**: a couple of hundred increments against a couple of thousand F2 points. That ringing is the vertical streaking through every peak that makes a benchtop 2D hard to read.

Measured on the real NOESY, off-peak F1 intensity as a fraction of the peak: **0.255 with no window, 0.098 with a cosine-bell.** And an independent confirmation fell out of it -- with the window on, the F1 peak moves to **4.74 ppm, exactly matching F2's**, i.e. dead on the diagonal. (Without it the ringing dragged the F1 maximum to 4.61.)

`read_2d` takes `window_f1`/`window_kwargs_f1`, defaulting to **None**, so no dataset already on disk changes on reload without the caller asking. The GUI gets **Window F1 / F1 LB / F1 SSB** as their own controls rather than re-targeting F2's through `dim_combo`: F1's truncate and zero-fill are already separate widgets, and a heavy sine-bell on 200 increments beside a light exponential on 2048 points is the normal case, not an exception. The choice persists and restores per spectrum like every other live control, and folds into the reader kwargs on reopen so the two pipelines cannot diverge.

### The envelope is drawn on F1's panel now

F2's panel has always carried the window's own shape over the FID. F1's, added last round, passed `window_envelope=None` -- on the grounds that F1 had no window, which was the other half of the same complaint. It now draws `_compute_f1_window_envelope`, so there is a way to see what Window F1 is doing, or that it is doing nothing.

### Two bugs the new tests caught, both mine from last round

* **F1 was halved again on every live rebuild.** `si1` is the length of the interferogram going *into* the transform, but both the live fallback and the Zero-fill F1 box seeded it from `spectrum.data.shape[0]` -- the row count *after* the transform. Correct while those were equal; wrong the moment TPPI started dropping the mirror half, so a 16-increment dataset went 16 -> 9 on load and then 9 -> 5 on the next control change. Inverted (`2 * (rows - 1)`) in both places, gated on `f1_transform`, so nothing else moves.
* **The restored F1 window was thrown away immediately.** `_populate_window_f1_combo` resets the combo to its first entry and was being called *after* the restore block (beside F2's own populate, which happens later in the method), so every reselection came back on "None" although the metadata held the right value. Moved above the restore.

### Tests

`tests/test_plotting_twod.py` +3: both axes increasing in the negative screen direction, a self-correlation landing on the drawn nQ = 1 line in display coordinates, and a pseudo-2D still counting slices upward. `tests/test_xpulse.py` +2: an F1 window actually suppressing truncation ringing (measured **half a bin off an exact FFT bin** on purpose -- on an exact bin a truncated transform leaks 3e-07 and there is nothing for a window to improve, which is the degenerate case, not the real one), and the default still being no window at all. `tests/test_gui.py` +4: the controls driving the live rebuild, the choice surviving reselection, the envelope's shape, and the saved state folding into the reader kwargs with "none" mapping to nothing rather than to a zero-width exponential.

## X-Pulse NOESY_HH wouldn't open, and the browser said everything twice (2026-09-18, seventeenth round)

User: "You were fixing the double noting of the experiment details above the folder browser since it is already noted in the selected spectrum part. And then I'm not able to open a 2D NOESY from x-pulse with the following error: spectral width (F1) must be > 0 to compute dt."

### The details panel above the folder browser is gone

It restated the selected experiment's nucleus, size and pulse programme -- all of which the Data tab's **"Selected spectrum"** box already prints (`_refresh_selection_display`), and each tree row already carries its own one-line summary from `DataBrowser._describe`. Three statements of the same facts on one tab. Removed, with a comment where it stood so it is not reintroduced; `_describe`'s own pulse-programme addition stays, since that is the row summary and not the duplicate.

### `SW1` is a sequence parameter, and not every sequence has one

`read_2d` read F1's spectral width from `exp_params["SW1"]` alone. That comes from the sequence's ParameterBlock, so it exists only where its author put it: `HSQC_HX` has one, **`NOESY_HH` does not** -- a homonuclear indirect window is not independently settable, it is swept at the direct dimension's rate. So the read died before producing anything, on a file that states its F1 dwell time perfectly well.

It states it in the NTUPLES header. `##FIRST=`/`##LAST=` give the T1 axis's endpoints in seconds and the page pairs are one per complex T1 increment, uniformly spaced (the per-page `T1` checkpoints step by a constant -- checked). So `dt1 = (t1_last - t1_first) / (n1 - 1)`.

**Checked against the one file that records both, not just asserted.** Quinine `HSQC_HX` has `SW1= 4000.0` and a T1 axis of 6e-06 -> 0.031756 s over 128 pairs: 0.03175/127 = 2.5e-04 s = **4000.0000 Hz, exact**. The `NOESY_HH` gives 6e-06 -> 0.127506 s over 256 pairs = **2000.0000 Hz**, which is also its `Filter` (the F2 window) to the digit -- exactly what a homonuclear F1 should be. A recorded `SW1` still wins where there is one: deriving over the top of it would hide a real mismatch rather than show it.

### A parsing bug the derivation immediately exposed

`##FIRST=` appears **twice before the first `##PAGE=`**: the real declaration, then the all-zero per-page placeholder. The reader's guard was `current_page is None`, which both satisfy, so last-wins overwrote the declaration with zeros -- while the function's own docstring said it used the first. Invisible for as long as only T2 was read off it (T2's first value genuinely is 0) and wrong the moment T1 was: T1's first value is the initial evolution time, 6e-06 s. Now first-wins, and the synthetic fixture carries a non-zero T1 `##FIRST=` on purpose, because a zero there would not have caught this.

### `TxPPMX` is the X channel, and a homonuclear sequence has no X channel

`tx_ppm_f1` fell back to 0.0, so a NOESY's F1 would have been centred at 0 ppm while F2 sat at `TxPPM` = 5.0 -- the diagonal 5 ppm off the diagonal. F1 now takes F2's offset **when both dimensions are the same nucleus**. A heteronuclear file with no `TxPPMX` still falls back to 0.0: borrowing the 1H offset for a 13C axis is a guess, not a deduction.

### Both dimensions were mirrored, and the cause was the same misreading

User, after the file first opened: *"the same issue is happening here in the NOESY as with the HSQC from x-pulse, the spectra are like duplicated. I see all the peaks but reflected about the centre."* Correct, in **both** dimensions, and both from one wrong assumption.

**`##SYMBOL= T1, T2, R, I` means what it says.** R and I are the real and imaginary halves of *one* t2 FID. The reader treated them as a States cos/sin pair at two t1 points -- but both pages of a pair carry the **same** `##PAGE= T1=` value, and the file declares `##.ACQUISITION MODE= SIMULTANEOUS`, so they cannot be. Left unpaired, every row was real-valued, so each row's F2 transform was the FFT of a real signal and came back Hermitian.

Measured: the NOESY's F2 projection had equal-height peaks at **4.74 and 5.26 ppm** about its 5.00 ppm carrier; combining the halves collapses them to a single 4.74 ppm peak. On the Quinine HSQC the pair 4.05/5.95 collapses to **4.05** -- which is its OCH3 (3.95 ppm in the literature), so the surviving peak is the real one and 5.95 was the reflection. The reflection is now 0.5% of the peak on the NOESY.

**F1 is TPPI, not States-TPPI.** With the pages correctly read there is no second dataset left to pair, and the file says so outright (`##.ACQUISITION SCHEME= TPPI`): F1 sign discrimination comes from the 90-degree-per-increment phase ramp alone. That leaves the t1 series real and amplitude-modulated, so a complex F1 FFT mirrors it exactly as F2 was mirroring -- and displaces everything by `SW1/4`, because 90 degrees per dwell *is* a quarter cycle per dwell. Both effects were measured before being fixed: peaks landed in equal-height pairs at ±8.4 ppm from the NOESY diagonal, and 8.4 ppm at 59.7 MHz is 500 Hz, which is `SW1/4` for that file's 2000 Hz F1 window.

`processing.ft.tppi_f1_spectrum` does the right transform: real part, FFT, drop the mirror half, shift the axis down by `SW1/4`. **The F1 axis is therefore half as wide as `1/dt1`** (it spans `SW1/2`, centred on the transmitter) with about half as many points -- not a loss, since the discarded half held nothing but reflections. `peek` halves to match, because its contract is "the shape a load produces".

After it: the NOESY's strongest peak sits at F2 4.74 / F1 5.00, i.e. on the diagonal to within 0.26 ppm, which is two F1 bins.

**`fn_mode` is now 3, not 5** -- Bruker's own FnMODE code for TPPI. That matters because the GUI keeps a *second* F1 pipeline (`_recompute_multi_row_data`) keyed on the same value, and a reader-only fix would have been undone by it the moment any control was touched. Both now route through the one helper. `_phase_needs_raw_rebuild` gains 3 as well: a TPPI F1 transform takes the real part of the F2 spectrum, so the stored plane has lost F2's imaginary part exactly as a hypercomplex decode's has.

**The old synthetic fixture was part of the problem.** It built States cos/sin pairs -- i.e. it modelled what the reader did rather than what the files contain -- so it agreed with the reader while both were wrong, and mirrored spectra passed every test. It now builds genuine TPPI (one complex t2 FID per t1 value, split into R and I pages, with the 90-degree ramp) and carries a known frequency in **both** dimensions, so a reflection in either fails.

### F1 now has an FID panel too

User: *"F1 processing doesn't show fid and spectrum, can this be done?"* Yes. `_show_2d_indirect_processing_preview` drew only the spectrum, on the stated grounds that "F1 has no window/shift/echo/LP controls of its own to judge against a raw trace" -- which overlooked the two F1 controls that do exist, **Truncate (F1) and Zero-fill (F1)**, both of which are decisions about where an interferogram has decayed to nothing and both of which were being made blind.

The data was already there: every vendor's `read_2d` stashes the F2-processed rows as `raw["fid"]` (Bruker `fid_f2`, X-Pulse `f2_rows`), and a column of that array *is* the series F1's transform runs across. `_f1_interferogram` takes the strongest F2 column's real part -- real, because an amplitude-modulated F1 carries its t1 information there, the imaginary part being F2's quadrature. `_recompute_multi_row_data` now refreshes `raw["fid"]` at the point it holds exactly that array, so the panel cannot show the interferogram of a spectrum that has since been reprocessed.

### Also fixed on the way: 18 stale test failures already in the working tree

Not from this round's work -- they were failing before it started, and both causes were assertions that had not kept up with an earlier round's own refactor.

* **Four `peek` tests** compared the whole dict with `==` and had not been given the `pulse_program` key `peek` now returns for every vendor.
* **Fourteen Analysis tests** read `analysis_results_label`, but that label stopped carrying reports when each sub-tab was given its own: curve fits go to `curve_fit_summary_label`, DOSY to `dosy_results_label`, gradient calibration to `gradient_calibration_label`. The code was right and the tests were stale -- repointed per test, deliberately *not* by a blanket rename, because several other tests assert that label is **not** written to any more and a global replace would have silently inverted them.

### Tests

`tests/test_xpulse.py` +13: the helper's preference order, its derivation, its refusal to guess; the derived width reproducing the recorded one on real data; `t1_first`/`t1_last` being the declaration and not the placeholder; a fixture with no `$$SW1=` loading to the same F1 axis as one with it; the homonuclear offset fallback and the heteronuclear non-fallback; the error text naming both places it looked; the pages pairing into one complex FID; **both known frequencies recovered with nothing at either reflection** (the regression for the user's report); the F1 axis being half the sweep width; and the same no-reflection check on real data. `tests/test_gui.py` +2 (the F1 interferogram, and its absence rather than a fake one when no rows are cached), plus the X-Pulse row-count assertions updated for TPPI's halving and the GUI's own NTUPLES fixture rebuilt on the true model. `tests/test_data_browser.py` -2 (the removed panel's own tests).


## Per-slice phases lost on reload, contour line width, and getting back to a DOSY (2026-09-16, sixteenth round)

Six items, two of them marked by the user as future work.

### Per-slice phasing was recorded and never applied

*"Need to make sure that per-slice phasing/processing is being maintained across loads."* It was not.

`slice_phase0`/`slice_phase1` were saved to the processing sidecar and restored into `metadata.raw` correctly -- and then nothing applied them. `_read_already_applied_saved_processing` returns True whenever the reader was handed the saved settings, but **the reader has no parameter for a per-slice phase**: it is a GUI concept (Autophase with "Apply to every slice", or a phase dragged on one slice), applied by `_recompute_multi_row_data`. So the load took the fast path and skipped them.

Measured: a 6-row raw 2D given per-slice phases of 10..60 degrees, saved and reloaded, came back differing from what had been stored by **24.7 of full scale** -- the phases recorded in metadata and absent from the data.

Fixed exactly as the user's own F1 phase already was: a non-zero slice phase excludes the fast path. Conditional, not blanket -- a series with no slice phases keeps the fast load, or this would undo the load-speed work.

### Contour line width

`plot_2d_contour`, `overlay_plot`, `plot_dosy` and `overlay_dosy` all hard-coded their ring weight. Now `contour_linewidth`, carried through `_contour_style_kwargs` and editable in the Plot Style dialog.

Deliberately **not** merged with `_AXIS_LINEWIDTH`: that styles axis furniture, and at its 1.75 default the rings come out heavy enough to merge into blobs -- which is why it was never forwarded in the first place. In `plot_dosy` the rings and the projection strip are separately weighted for the same reason.

A contour's width lives on the `QuadContourSet` matplotlib builds from the levels, so unlike a trace colour it cannot be set on what is already drawn -- `set_style` rebuilds.

### Getting back to a DOSY

*"Still no way to get back to the previous DOSY ILT."* The inversions list was gated on `len(variants) > 1`, on the reasoning that a single inversion is already on screen. But the Fit canvas is shared with the curve fit, SCORE and eNMR, so running any of those left the one DOSY with nothing to bring it back. Now shown at one or more.

**Not built: the general "modules in the Fit tab" system the user proposed.** `self.fit_canvas` is referenced as a tab *widget* in 16 places and 98 test sites, so hosting a sub-tab bar inside it means unpicking all of that -- a round of its own, not a fix alongside five others. What landed addresses the symptom; the general version (a results bar accumulating DOSY / curve fit / SCORE / eNMR entries) is still open.

### Already done

*"Changing series colour map should redraw the existing plot"* -- landed in the fifteenth round, the turn before it was reported. Verified: the drawn line colours change, not only the stored series.

### Noted for future, at the user's own request
